First off, welcome to the thread!

I'm also on the red path and I briefly discussed this as well in my earlier post.
As I mentioned there, to me it seems that everyone, including Ami, Himawari, Nao-chan, HOPE, Pareidolia, Yasu's god, Kaori, Sekai, literally anyone with some form of devine knowledge, is highlighting how important it is that Akira has sex with all the girls.
That would, obviously, include Ami, and since the good uncle Akira refuses to do so, it infuriates her.

I interpret her definition of salvation as whatever is planned as end game content, possibly the "true end".
Meaning that only once Akira stops being "a baby-back bitch" and decides to sex the whole cast will he be able to reach the point that he is inevitably supposed to reach.

The question whether he is the "real" Akira is a complicated one for me though.
What defines the "real" Akira? For Maya, it is the Akira that has the same memories and characteristics that the one from her original world. Even then, I don't think it necessarily has to be literally that body of flesh from that world. We don't even know what happened to that "original" Akira that Maya knows. For all we know he might have died a long time ago.
Similarly, I don't think there really is a point in defining a "real" Akira for Ami. She at least doesn't seem to care. All she cares for is that this version of Akira gets himself to where he is supposed to go, actively "helping" him in that, like with kidnapping Karin to finally get him to fuck her, since she realized during their conversation that Karin might mature too quickly, becoming less prone to manipulation and possibly prolong the process further.

To me personally, there are no "real" or "fake" Akiras. Neither are there any "real" or "fake" Mayas, Amis, Nodokas, you name it.
There are millions of worlds with millions of versions of sorts of characters. And as Himawari put it, in one way or another, you really just cheer for each of them to find their own place of pure happiness.

Hey brothers, I just started playing this game last month and I’m currently in Chapter 4. I've realized that I missed quite a few events along the way.

Does anyone have tips or a better way to keep track of these branching paths? I’d really appreciate some advice so I don't mess up my run further!

"I apologize in advance if I’ve overlooked something obvious."
Click to expand...
It's pretty simple really - the green path is called the green path because it's the playthrough that lets you see every event (so all the events are green once you're done). Red is red because missed events are red. If you're already in chapter 4 you'll probably continue to miss events because you've already passed most of the choices and some of them have continuous consequences.

Using the guide mod should allow you to stay on the right path pretty easily, are there any specific examples you can give? Maybe there's a common thread and they stem from the same thing.

As a general rule of thumb staying on the green path mostly just means saying "yes" to doing anything. Should I fuck someone? Yes. Should I lie to Karin? Yes. Should I go in the bathroom with Chinami? Yes. There's only three exceptions to this rule of thumb that I can think of, but you're well past them at this point.

this is what happens when you are missing the scene data for the specific events. the game is trying to call the data of the events you are playing, but cannot find them in your game folder. this usually happens when you manually update the game version by version, but mistakingly skipping an update on your way to the latest one. for example, this happened to me when i was on a .52 version then updating to .54, which meant i never got the .53 data installed, hence the screen showing me, quite literally, that "there is nothing."

just quickly back up your saves and carefully install the individual version updates again, or even do a fresh install of .56.1 in its entirety.

posts.content_html_raw:
Okay, so, hopefully this question won’t be seen as either accusatory or inflammatory, because I *do* genuinely only seek to understand, but it’s something that has been on my mind for quite a while now: what do you – people like me, who have (un)willingly sold their soul to Selebus and spent multiple months (or, in many cases, multiple years) engaging with this particular unholy piece of fiction – actually want from it?

Because for the last two or so years (or maybe it began even earlier – I don’t really remember, since at this point half of the length of this thread is *just* the discussion of Chapter 4 alone, even if it's still only half-complete) whenever a new update comes around there almost always ends up being a decently large number of people who describe it as “mostly meaningless, empty and boring” and state that they are “rapidly losing their interest in the story”.

And, just to be perfectly clear, this isn’t me blaming people for not enjoying the narrative, or anything like that: these are the matters of personal opinions, and individual tastes, and yada-yada-yada – yet I am still extremely fascinated by these criticisms, because they vividly showcase that even among the long-time fans who have stuck with Selebus’ creation for many years there is no proper consensus on what the actual “appeal” of Lessons in Love really is, aside from just some vague notion of it having “very good character writing”. Pretty much everyone agrees that it’s not the “porn” aspect of it, sure – but beyond that? What is inherently appealing to some (the “meta” and “horror” narrative elements, slow-burn romance and slice-of-life scenes, unfair puzzles, long-winded philosophical monologues, loads of metaphors and symbolism, wizard content) is equally off-putting – or, alternatively, just flat-out boring – to others, leading to this exact weird unfortunate situation, where outside of some extremely rare exceptions (like 0.53) a decent amount of people are inevitably going to be disappointed *no matter what* Selebus does.

For me personally, I already mentioned at one point that the singular absolute virtue I believe in life is “authenticity”, and so the thing that appeals to me the most in fiction is characters being unapologetically genuine with themselves or each other, whether in the form of accepting their “inner shadow”, openly showing their vulnerability to another person or temporarily taking off their mask and expressing how they *truly* feel. From that standpoint, just in this last 0.56 update we had: two touching heart-to-heart scenes (Wakana/Akira and Akira/Niki), four less touching, but still very insightful scenes where the characters openly talked about their feelings (Wakana/Rika/Imani, Kirin/Karin, Karin/Ami, Niki/Noriko), as well as two-and-a-half great “mask off” scenes (Ami/Noriko and Ami/Sensei, the latter of which differs *greatly* depending on the Green/Red Path) – which is why I greatly enjoyed 0.56 as a whole. However, from what I’ve seen over the course of these last six days, most people in this thread didn’t really care for either Ami or Karin/Kirin scenes, mostly liked the stuff with Wakana and Niki, had a lot to say about Chinami’s TSS (justifiably: it was really well-written) and were either ambivalent or outright negative in regards to everything else – which, once again, is not me pointing fingers or criticizing anybody, but simply substantiating what I stated in my previous paragraph with some actual examples.

And so, Da Capo – it all returns back to the beginning, to my original question. To you, the person who is reading this post: what do *you* think is the biggest appeal of LiL? What makes this particular story so appealing to *you* personally, so that you are compelled to return to it again, and again, and again for God knows how many months in a row at this point (outside of, like, sunk cost fallacy)?

I'm between both DeSkel and Bingoogus at this point. I'm still very curious in the story, and how the characters will continue to grow, and the mysteries surrounding everything. What's going on with the upside down house, how everything connects in this world, what the real meaning of the loops and gods is/are.

I also do love all the characters after seeing them grow after all these years? I want to see them succeed and redeem themselves. That's why I'm disappointed when progress feels rushed, because this game is a slice of life at times and when Akira suddenly fingerbangs Touka for 5 minutes with a lot more bluntness than I expect, I feel a bit cheated because there's been a lot of "will they/won't they/when will they" and then it just suddenly happens. Maybe I have brain worms and am forgetting a few more teasing scenes but it did seem pretty abrupt to me.

I also want to see Akira finally get caught for all the shit he's doing, and the inevitable spiral, because he simply can't get away with this forever. And then I want to see his redemption as well. Or a resolution. Something justifiable.

It's certainly sunk cost at this point, too. I absolutely need to see how Sel ends the story, and I'm still hoping it'll all come together nicely.

Why do I personally keep playing the game?
I'm a sucker for mystery stories. Stories where there's an interesting premise with solid world building and well-written and distinct characters, sprinkled with some well-nuanced humor.
All these aspects apply to this game. Although, at this point, I would even disregard calling it a game, because it essentially evolved into more of a kinetic novel (considering there is a single canon path as per the creator himself) than something truly interactive.

And as such, I would compare it rather to a TV show or a book series. Only that, as other people pointed out, the sheer amount of content far outshines most, if not any, existing book series, let alone TV show.
Which is another selling point in itself: The regularity of new content.
Whereas most book series (GRR Martin, anyone?) and many TV shows take years for new books/seasons to be published, this format enables monthly updates of decently sized content, keeping your interest fresh. I could imagine myself simply forgetting about it after waiting for a new update for a few months. Which mind you, still happens at times, but once I come back, I get to play 2-3 months worth of updates which re-kindle the fire within me.

And I believe the last paragraph broadly sums up the general success of this game. It's good and reliable, sometimes that's all it takes.
Because, and please don't take it personally, your post almost sounds like a cry for approval from other people to acknowledge its quality. But just like with any other media property, there will be people enjoying different parts of it, prioritizing some over the other, being able to appreciate some nuances while overlooking others. That's the nature of humans. Everyone has their own taste.
I myself also practically faint in disbelief whenever someone tells me they weren't able to get into some of my favorite movies, shows or books, explaining they found them boring or whatever. "You philistine, how can you besmudge the reputation of such magnificent works of art with your petty ignorance?!", I'd like to respond. But then I think for a second and have to realize that I probably also disliked some things that a majority of others consider amazing and above all else. That's just how it goes, there is no real objectivity when it comes to art, or almost anything that cannot be empirically measured, really.

So to sum it up: Taste is subjective, you can like something for different reasons and it's all valid, nobody has to agree with everything and see it the same way that others do, what's important is that, as DeSkel rightfully pointed out, you feel something.
Whether the urge and curiosity to see its conclusion, the excitement of seeing your favorite character's arc evolve and their character grow as a consequence, the fact that you get to see wizard sex (a surprisingly high amount of people I just recently noticed) or just to follow its development and wait for an opportunity to be able to criticize an arrogant prick of a developer for how he fucked something up and garner satisfaction solely from that.

Because at the end of the day, whether you decide to write about how much you liked an update or whether you come here to complain about it or write a 1-star review, or whether you just lurk and read people's opinions about it to better understand the story or further collect context and deepen your enjoyment of the story - you choose to interact because it made you feel something.

Okay, so, hopefully this question won’t be seen as either accusatory or inflammatory, because I *do* genuinely only seek to understand, but it’s something that has been on my mind for quite a while now: what do you – people like me, who have (un)willingly sold their soul to Selebus and spent multiple months (or, in many cases, multiple years) engaging with this particular unholy piece of fiction – actually want from it?
Spoiler:
Further elaboration
Because for the last two or so years (or maybe it began even earlier – I don’t really remember, since at this point half of the length of this thread is *just* the discussion of Chapter 4 alone, even if it's still only half-complete) whenever a new update comes around there almost always ends up being a decently large number of people who describe it as “mostly meaningless, empty and boring” and state that they are “rapidly losing their interest in the story”.
And, just to be perfectly clear, this isn’t me blaming people for not enjoying the narrative, or anything like that: these are the matters of personal opinions, and individual tastes, and yada-yada-yada – yet I am still extremely fascinated by these criticisms, because they vividly showcase that even among the long-time fans who have stuck with Selebus’ creation for many years there is no proper consensus on what the actual “appeal” of Lessons in Love really is, aside from just some vague notion of it having “very good character writing”. Pretty much everyone agrees that it’s not the “porn” aspect of it, sure – but beyond that? What is inherently appealing to some (the “meta” and “horror” narrative elements, slow-burn romance and slice-of-life scenes, unfair puzzles, long-winded philosophical monologues, loads of metaphors and symbolism, wizard content) is equally off-putting – or, alternatively, just flat-out boring – to others, leading to this exact weird unfortunate situation, where outside of some extremely rare exceptions (like 0.53) a decent amount of people are inevitably going to be disappointed *no matter what* Selebus does.
For me personally, I already mentioned at one point that the singular absolute virtue I believe in life is “authenticity”, and so the thing that appeals to me the most in fiction is characters being unapologetically genuine with themselves or each other, whether in the form of accepting their “inner shadow”, openly showing their vulnerability to another person or temporarily taking off their mask and expressing how they *truly* feel. From that standpoint, just in this last 0.56 update we had: two touching heart-to-heart scenes (Wakana/Akira and Akira/Niki), four less touching, but still very insightful scenes where the characters openly talked about their feelings (Wakana/Rika/Imani, Kirin/Karin, Karin/Ami, Niki/Noriko), as well as two-and-a-half great “mask off” scenes (Ami/Noriko and Ami/Sensei, the latter of which differs *greatly* depending on the Green/Red Path) – which is why I greatly enjoyed 0.56 as a whole. However, from what I’ve seen over the course of these last six days, most people in this thread didn’t really care for either Ami or Karin/Kirin scenes, mostly liked the stuff with Wakana and Niki, had a lot to say about Chinami’s TSS (justifiably: it was really well-written) and were either ambivalent or outright negative in regards to everything else – which, once again, is not me pointing fingers or criticizing anybody, but simply substantiating what I stated in my previous paragraph with some actual examples.
And so, Da Capo – it all returns back to the beginning, to my original question. To you, the person who is reading this post: what do *you* think is the biggest appeal of LiL? What makes this particular story so appealing to *you* personally, so that you are compelled to return to it again, and again, and again for God knows how many months in a row at this point (outside of, like, sunk cost fallacy)?

I personally
keep playing the game?

All these aspects apply to this game. Although, at this point, I would even disregard calling it a game, because it essentially evolved into more of a kinetic novel (considering there
is
a single canon path as per the creator himself) than something truly interactive.
And as such, I would compare it rather to a TV show or a book series. Only that, as other people pointed out, the sheer amount of content far outshines most, if not any, existing book series, let alone TV show.
Which is another selling point in itself: The regularity of new content.
Whereas most book series (GRR Martin, anyone?) and many TV shows take years for new books/seasons to be published, this format enables monthly updates of decently sized content, keeping your interest fresh. I could imagine myself simply forgetting about it after waiting for a new update for a few months. Which mind you, still happens at times, but once I come back, I get to play 2-3 months worth of updates which re-kindle the fire within me.
And I believe the last paragraph broadly sums up the general success of this game. It's good and reliable, sometimes that's all it takes.
Because, and please don't take it personally, your post almost sounds like a cry for approval from other people to acknowledge its quality. That's the nature of humans. Everyone has their own taste.
I myself also practically faint in disbelief whenever someone tells me they weren't able to get into some of my favorite movies, shows or books, explaining they found them boring or whatever. "You philistine, how can you besmudge the reputation of such magnificent works of art with your petty ignorance?!", I'd like to respond. That's just how it goes, there is no real objectivity when it comes to art, or almost anything that cannot be empirically measured, really.

something

CharlotteWiltshire26 said:
what do you – people like me, who have (un)willingly sold their soul to Selebus and spent multiple months (or, in many cases, multiple years) engaging with this particular unholy piece of fiction – actually want from it?
Click to expand...
For Ami to suffer, of course.

Aside from that the biggest appeal to me is just the writing - by which I don't mean the story itself, though I love that too. The quality of the piece-by-piece writing is just so high and so much higher than its peers I couldn't not enjoy LiL, I don't think. In contrast to some others here I think I could only really point to one or two updates where that didn't really hold true for me (namely 0.49, the last dorm wars), though I haven't been following along for years yet and I don't look into anything Sel says or does so the fact that those points don't factor in for me might help.

I also just love the cast. Juggling a cast this size is just downright impressive and whilst I have a few complaints for a few of the characters (e.g Miku's current devolution into a childish sex joke machine) overall I just love the cast right the way through, even the characters I hate. So part of the appeal is just to continue seeing them and seeing where their stories go.

Another huge appeal to me is just the subject matter, especially lately. One of the really cool things for me about VN's in general is that they can feature/explore certain subject matters that conventional media just won't. The particular cycle of abuse at play in LiL and the pathology behind are really interesting to me. There's probably an episode or two of SVU or something where Stabler and Ice T explain it to a degree whilst discussing the pros and cons of just beating men like Akira to death but that's about it lol putting the player in Akira's shoes in an explicit story is just far more engaging to me than something like that.

Also I just like weird shit, and LiL is my brand of weird shit. Love Kumon-mi, love all the happy events, love moyo and her cum-bucket. I've always been good at divorcing fiction from reality and I have a high threshold for "dark" so nothing in the game so far has really phased me at all or put me off. Honestly the only part of the game that doesn't appeal to me are the sex scenes and I can just skip through them so I don't have a reason not to stick around right now, though I am dreading the inevitable wizardy.

Because for the last two or so years (or maybe it began even earlier – I don’t really remember, since at this point half of the length of this thread is *just* the discussion of Chapter 4 alone, even if it's still only half-complete) whenever a new update comes around there almost always ends up being a decently large number of people who describe it as “mostly meaningless, empty and boring” and state that they are “rapidly losing their interest in the story”.

And, just to be perfectly clear, this isn’t me blaming people for not enjoying the narrative, or anything like that: these are the matters of personal opinions, and individual tastes, and yada-yada-yada – yet I am still extremely fascinated by these criticisms, because they vividly showcase that even among the long-time fans who have stuck with Selebus’ creation for many years there is no proper consensus on what the actual “appeal” of Lessons in Love really is, aside from just some vague notion of it having “very good character writing”. Pretty much everyone agrees that it’s not the “porn” aspect of it, sure – but beyond that? What is inherently appealing to some (the “meta” and “horror” narrative elements, slow-burn romance and slice-of-life scenes, unfair puzzles, long-winded philosophical monologues, loads of metaphors and symbolism, wizard content) is equally off-putting – or, alternatively, just flat-out boring – to others, leading to this exact weird unfortunate situation, where outside of some extremely rare exceptions (like 0.53) a decent amount of people are inevitably going to be disappointed *no matter what* Selebus does.

For me personally, I already mentioned at one point that the singular absolute virtue I believe in life is “authenticity”, and so the thing that appeals to me the most in fiction is characters being unapologetically genuine with themselves or each other, whether in the form of accepting their “inner shadow”, openly showing their vulnerability to another person or temporarily taking off their mask and expressing how they *truly* feel. From that standpoint, just in this last 0.56 update we had: two touching heart-to-heart scenes (Wakana/Akira and Akira/Niki), four less touching, but still very insightful scenes where the characters openly talked about their feelings (Wakana/Rika/Imani, Kirin/Karin, Karin/Ami, Niki/Noriko), as well as two-and-a-half great “mask off” scenes (Ami/Noriko and Ami/Sensei, the latter of which differs *greatly* depending on the Green/Red Path) – which is why I greatly enjoyed 0.56 as a whole. However, from what I’ve seen over the course of these last six days, most people in this thread didn’t really care for either Ami or Karin/Kirin scenes, mostly liked the stuff with Wakana and Niki, had a lot to say about Chinami’s TSS (justifiably: it was really well-written) and were either ambivalent or outright negative in regards to everything else – which, once again, is not me pointing fingers or criticizing anybody, but simply substantiating what I stated in my previous paragraph with some actual examples.

And so, Da Capo – it all returns back to the beginning, to my original question. To you, the person who is reading this post: what do *you* think is the biggest appeal of LiL? What makes this particular story so appealing to *you* personally, so that you are compelled to return to it again, and again, and again for God knows how many months in a row at this point (outside of, like, sunk cost fallacy)?

Great quality question!

So, I started my LIL journey in September, catching up at the start of 0.54 after 200 hours...so, my journey has not been one of years, thankfully.

I think, ultimately, because I got to have such a large bulk of the game ready for me to enjoy...I don't see most of the negatives that seem to bog down the enjoyment that those that have been waiting for years.

Long winded philosophical rants? That's part of Akira, and the various Gods characters. I've mostly enjoyed these, as it does add to the games vibe as a whole.

The puzzles are the weakest bits in my opinion, and absolutely would be done without them. The only one I bothered with without using the guide was the liminal mall, and that's because it was interesting.

Outside of that? I see most of the parts of the game as they are, as a whole, as entertaining. There is a will they/won't they energy to a lot of stuff. There is slow and fast burn. There is romance, and love, and lust and mystery and horror and SO! MUCH! LORE!

It truly has everything a book lover could ever want...while also featuring h scenes. The cast is great, with character growth that for the most part feels very genuine. It's reasonable when needed, and absurd in the best ways possible...which fits the vibes because the game itself is set in an absurd world.

I've laughed, I've cried, I've gagged, I've cringed. I've sat in awe and wonder! I've regretted and been vindicated...

And it's only halfway done?

If the second half, is half as good as the first half? We're eating fucking good.

As a whole, this VN will certainly be considered one of the greatest of all time. I get to be part of that journey! That's worth it to me...even if I have to be trickled content month after month, chomping at the bit.

Plus...I enjoy the community. Most of you all are cool, and talking with you all, asking questions, polling opinions, and theory crafting over the past few months has been a lot of fun.

Over all? I'm enjoying the game. I think, if you're tired of the game at this point...you should take a few months off. Maybe even a year. Come back when there is a lot of new content to enjoy, maybe even do a full restart while you wait? Experience the entire thing over again, see how it all fits together all over again!

So much has been added, slowly over time, that some of your pain points may not even be a thing anymore.

What is inherently appealing to some (the “meta” and “horror” narrative elements, slow-burn romance and slice-of-life scenes, unfair puzzles, long-winded philosophical monologues, loads of metaphors and symbolism, wizard content) is equally off-putting – or, alternatively, just flat-out boring – to others, leading to this exact weird unfortunate situation, where outside of some extremely rare exceptions (like 0.53) a decent amount of people are inevitably going to be disappointed *no matter what* Selebus does.
For me personally, I already mentioned at one point that the singular absolute virtue I believe in life is “authenticity”, and so the thing that appeals to me the most in fiction is characters being unapologetically genuine with themselves or each other, whether in the form of accepting their “inner shadow”, openly showing their vulnerability to another person or temporarily taking off their mask and expressing how they *truly* feel. From that standpoint, just in this last 0.56 update we had: two touching heart-to-heart scenes (Wakana/Akira and Akira/Niki), four less touching, but still very insightful scenes where the characters openly talked about their feelings (Wakana/Rika/Imani, Kirin/Karin, Karin/Ami, Niki/Noriko), as well as two-and-a-half great “mask off” scenes (Ami/Noriko and Ami/Sensei, the latter of which differs *greatly* depending on the Green/Red Path) – which is why I greatly enjoyed 0.56 as a whole. However, from what I’ve seen over the course of these last six days, most people in this thread didn’t really care for either Ami or Karin/Kirin scenes, mostly liked the stuff with Wakana and Niki, had a lot to say about Chinami’s TSS (justifiably: it was really well-written) and were either ambivalent or outright negative in regards to everything else – which, once again, is not me pointing fingers or criticizing anybody, but simply substantiating what I stated in my previous paragraph with some actual examples.
And so, Da Capo – it all returns back to the beginning, to my original question. To you, the person who is reading this post: what do *you* think is the biggest appeal of LiL? What makes this particular story so appealing to *you* personally, so that you are compelled to return to it again, and again, and again for God knows how many months in a row at this point (outside of, like, sunk cost fallacy)?
Click to expand...
Great quality question!
So, I started my LIL journey in September, catching up at the start of 0.54 after 200 hours...so, my journey has not been one of years, thankfully.
I think, ultimately, because I got to have such a large bulk of the game ready for me to enjoy...I don't see most of the negatives that seem to bog down the enjoyment that those that have been waiting for years.
Long winded philosophical rants? That's part of Akira, and the various Gods characters. I've mostly enjoyed these, as it does add to the games vibe as a whole.
The puzzles are the weakest bits in my opinion, and absolutely would be done without them. The only one I bothered with without using the guide was the liminal mall, and that's because it was interesting.
Outside of that? I see most of the parts of the game as they are, as a whole, as entertaining. There is a will they/won't they energy to a lot of stuff. There is slow and fast burn. There is romance, and love, and lust and mystery and horror and SO! MUCH! LORE!
It truly has everything a book lover could ever want...while also featuring h scenes. The cast is great, with character growth that for the most part feels very genuine. It's reasonable when needed, and absurd in the best ways possible...which fits the vibes because the game itself is set in an absurd world.
I've laughed, I've cried, I've gagged, I've cringed. I've sat in awe and wonder! I've regretted and been vindicated...
And it's only halfway done?
If the second half, is half as good as the first half? We're eating fucking good.
As a whole, this VN will certainly be considered one of the greatest of all time. I get to be part of that journey! That's worth it to me...even if I have to be trickled content month after month, chomping at the bit.
Plus...I enjoy the community. Most of you all are cool, and talking with you all, asking questions, polling opinions, and theory crafting over the past few months has been a lot of fun.
Over all? I'm enjoying the game. I think, if you're tired of the game at this point...you should take a few months off. Maybe even a year. Come back when there is a lot of new content to enjoy, maybe even do a full restart while you wait? Experience the entire thing over again, see how it all fits together all over again!
So much has been added, slowly over time, that some of your pain points may not even be a thing anymore.

If you're asking in terms of continuity though there's no strict chronological order outside of instances where an event has pre-requisite events.

The way the game is structured in most areas is that there's a batch of event lines you can do in mostly whatever order you want and the last event in those lines will be pre-requisites for a smaller number of event chains that will then converge on a holiday and then from there the game branches outwards again with a small number and then those branch into a larger number and then it shrinks again.

So yeah, the AutoVN mod obviously has made an orderly list but technically you could swap events round in a bunch of places since they're mostly self-contained. At the start of chapter 1 for example you could start with Ami's first two events, or Rin's, or Futaba's, or Ayane's, etc. and there's nothing in any of them to suggest which comes before which so how you'd order them is completely trivial. Even the main events in chapter 1 aren't likely to all be tackled sequentially.

just starting out, but what is the care pakage?
and what is all this extra stuff? like the fan signature or the auto vn. should i just play the main game or should i also download some of the stuff from other links?
sorry for the dumb and uncultured question, thanks.
Click to expand...
Nah, don't worry. Just download the base game (and the hotfix for this version only if you haven't yet), the one that says Guide Mod, and the one that says Naming Save Mod. Those are the basic ones so you don't rage at other things that aren't the game itself. The guide mod gets updated with the public release of an update, generally 15-20 days after every game update here.
As for the rest of the extra stuff, it's mostly just extra stuff, as it says. AutoVN Mod pretty much forces linear mode to the game. Dark Mode makes the UI dark (the game itself can still lightbomb you sometimes), Cheat Code is a list of cheats (careful, it marks you as a cheater, and that has consequences), Cheat Mod lets you set some values without being marked as a cheater, Puzzle Guide is a guide to the puzzles that appear in the game (if you DO end up playing it past the first 5 hours, remember this guide), Trigger Guide is a walkthrough to see scenes in latter updates, tends to get updated on the same day of the update, faster than the guide mod, FanFest 2025 is a formerly-free paid DLC with bonus "non-canon" content, same as the Care Packages, which, as mentioned by another post, are paid DLC with bonus "non-canon" content (though, as the spoiler itself says, if you install a care package, you also need to install the Disable DRM patch and reinstall it every time you update the game to a new version, or your saves and game will be deleted).

The rest of the extra content is translations to other languages and assets of the game characters, no idea how up-to-date they are, though.
Also, the focus of the game isn't in the sexual scenes, saying it just in case so you don't get any false expectations. You should still give it a go.

She is still aggressive, yes. Moreso, in some instances. The end result of the most significant scenes where this is the case is pretty much the same but her rants sometimes revolve around insulting Akira for his decision not to fuck her - generally speaking the ultimate outcome of the conversations will be the same but the conversation will be a bit different.

It's a fairly significant change overall, the dialogue in a lot of her scenes get changed and the dynamic of her and Akira's relationship is a bit different, especially through chapters 2 and 3. It's also worth noting it impacts events outside of just Ami as well - for example the second Nodokathon doesn't happen if you're not fucking Ami which then branches into several other missed events that have nothing to do with her. In total you miss a good 21 or so events (no doubt with more to miss in the future) and I think only 8 of them are actual Ami events.

If you're already that far into your green path playthrough I'd recommend just carrying on, even if you don't like Ami personally she's obviously a very important part of both Akira and the story overall and that will become clearer and clearer as you near the most recent update.

My personal opinion would be that anyone who's really into the game should do at least two playthroughs regardless and one of those should be a good uncle run. My second playthrough was as enjoyable as my first for all the extra stuff I picked up on and as far as the good uncle path itself goes there's a lot of interesting stuff to compare and contrast and it helps give a fuller picture of some things.

I'm bored at work. So I was thinking, this might be the first update in a little while without an obvious major bell-cow event.

0.53 had Aomori + huge lore dump

0.54 had post Aomori fallout, Maya Lore, Chika development, and Trash Wolf SA.

0.55 had big Touka moments, proposal snafus, and THE big Maki confrontation.

0.56 had Niki reunion, another big Ami confrontation, and more Noriko dubs.

0.57 seems lacking off rip compared to some of the events above.

Just to waste some more time at work, here are some ideas by character going by the tracker:

Uta - maybe some more throuple development? Could go in a couple different directions but I dont recall any prominent imminent drama on the horizon. My money is on relationship stuff + further lewding. Which now that I type that out lfg.

Molly - Same boat as Uta, albeit further along. I'm bettin some light hearted fun if Uta is the big relationship development, and the other candidates might be on more serious topics.

Miku - More Maki fallout. Maki saw right through the "older boyfriend" line so I gotta imagine that comes up. The dark room in the preview makes me think a good serious conversation with Akira after a blackout of sorts.

Sana + Sara - Lumping these 2 together cause we gotta have a full disclosure style event tween them and Akira sometime post Nadokathon nonsense. Normally this would be awesome, but Sana is evil now and I fear will only drag Sara down to her level. This is probably the "big one" of the update if I have to guess. Maybe we get some Haruka hints for Akira too.

In any case, it will be the opposite of wholesome given Sana's inclusion. I think these will leave us feeling icky.

Yuki - The palate cleanse events after the debauchery of Sana + Sara. I bet it'll be more growth tween her, Akira, and Yumi. Tsubasa might be in here too given her role. These will make us go "awww".

Kaori - Pure lore stuff + Sekai speech. We'll have some more T-pose fuckery too. Niki is involved somehow per the preview. Maybe Niki will intrude on everyones events given the big insta blowup? That'd be fun.

Noriko - Headpats for semi-best girl might be best headpats event. She could win at that at least. Tho Noriko has been doing really well lately event wise. Good for you Noriko.

I'm playing through the game again(Cause of course I am), and I just hit Chapter 2's event, "The Color White".

Yasu's little karaoke scene is so adorable, I love her so much. This scene does alot to set up Touka as the motherly type as well, as she's watching over Yasu during the christmas party. Sel's choice here to use a custom version of a song, and attribute it to Yasu singing is such a nice touch. It frames the other things happening around the hotel so well, like the Miku and Makoto scene outside.

It's actually easy to see that Sel really does know how to frame a scene well, build the emotions, and push you in the direction he wants emotionally. The game is so long, with such a large diverse cast that there are alot of smaller scenes that are easy to forget in the backdrop of the larger crazy moments.

Miku and the bear, for instance? It's such a sweet scene, but with the reset and other bullshit happening right around the corner(Including the mystery of 'is Ayane Preggo or not'), it's easy to forget about it.

Truly a wonder of a VN...

Because she got placed in that alt timeline that has a different set of events, that timeline (the alt one) briefly became her reality. Okay, I can’t believe that I – this thread’s resident Selebus glazer – am saying this, but the Ayane explanation feels like total bullshit to me. Not necessarily even due to the list “retcon” itself, but because this reveal further complicates what I already consider to be the single most contradictory and incomprehencible sequence of events in the entire game: the “middle” part of the fifth Halloween party, from “Even Gods Get Lost” to “All Around the Mulberry Bush” (as in, effectively the entire “timeline shenanigans” stuff that happens).

To anyone who cares to read further, be warned that this is going to be fairly long, since I have an entire section in my 2000+ pages of notes dedicated just to this one sequence specifically:

“All Around the Mulberry Bush” continues directly from the previous event, “Transpacific Sadness Symposium IV: TALKATIVE OBLONG MIRROR”, with Makoto reappearing back in the “real” Halloween Party – which the narrator calls “going to her real home” – seemingly right after Sensei has left with Nao-chan at the end of “Even Gods Get Lost”.

Still having all of the memories of what just happened: both the alternative timeline and her subsequent experience in the Transpacific Sadness Symposium – Makoto immediately tries to contact Sensei via her phone, but fails, as the call doesn’t go through. The girl then notices Ami and Maya, both of whom have also only just arrived to the party (and neither acting strangely in any way, implying that this is happening before Maya is sent to the other world), and tries to reach him via Ami’s phone instead – an attempt that also ultimately ends in complete failure.

Now, this is the part where things get very confusing, very fast:

To begin with, the fact that Makoto’s reappearance chronologically happens at the very end of the party, just after Sensei left, is incredibly strange in and of itself, as, with the exception of possible time lag/fuckery between different alternative worlds, we have no idea when she actually got sent to the other timeline in the first place. The only prior event that prominently features her is “Action/Inaction” in the very beginning of the event chain, and she can also briefly be seen next to Chika in the background of “Empty Heart Appeal”, when Sensei just arrives to the party. Other than that, however, Makoto is almost completely absent from any of the story scenes, and only returns to the spotlight in “Restart”, after the switch has already happened.

Even more importantly, however, the call made by Makoto via Ami’s phone is almost certainly the exact same call Sensei receives in the very beginning of “A House Near a Lake (The Same Place as Always)”, which brings the entire timeline of events of this Halloween Party into question:

The original order of events initially seemed to be:

“Sensei goes with Nao to the School” (“Even Gods Get Lost” / “A House Near A Lake”) -> “Sensei talks to Kaori/Pareidolia on the roof” (“Friend”) -> “Sensei has sex with Kaori after Pareidolia gets deleted” (“Kittens”) -> “SENSEI-QUEST” -> “The Orb/GOD consuming everything” (“Restart”) -> “Alternative world shenanigans” (“Recap”, and all the following events).

Yet “All Around the Mulberry Bush” happens after everything they have experienced in the “Sekai is alive” timeline, even though the call itself happens before “SENSEI-QUEST” and “Restart”.

So, what does this mean, exactly? Is this a different call and the event itself is a misdirection that is intentionally meant to confuse you, or did Makoto actually time-travel into the past using the “all changes that happen because of time travel have already happened and are accounted for, so you simply play them out as it has already happened” time-travel rules?

And if it’s the latter, what originally happened to Makoto during that Halloween party? Was (is?) there a version of her that actually got to experience the party before being transported into an alternative reality with Sensei, or did she always have her “consciousness replaced” by a future-version of her, that then acted out the events leading up to “SENSEI-QUEST” and then-then had her memories erased before being transported, thus “closing” the loop?

Or is this not the “original” reality, but a different one that is simply very close to it? Meaning that Makoto didn’t “go back in time”, but simply “switched lines” with the foreknowledge of what is going to happen next (thanks to her own timeline). But if so, then what the fuck was with the original phone call Sensei got in “Even the Gods Get Lost”? Was that actually Ami calling him that time?

Also, when Makoto realizes that both of her attempts to reach Sensei have ended in failure and that she has no other alternatives, the girl decides to do the next best thing and go talk to Ayane instead, to see whether she has experienced anything similar. To her dismay, Ayane also reacts with surprise and confusion when confronted with this revelation, which seems to imply that this version of Ayane is yet to experience the timeline switch and only going to go through it at some point in the near future – except for the fact that when the switch does happen, she never once mentions Makoto warning her about it, which either doesn’t mean anything or is a whole other can of worms that only complicates the timeline fuckery even further.

It is also notable that during the same conversation Makoto specifically points that it was *their* Sensei that she met in the other worldline (confirmed by the fact that in his inner narration he repeatedly mentions Pareidolia being gone, implying that this Sensei did indeed go through the events of “Friend”, “Kittens” and “SENSEI-QUEST”), which once again contradicts the supposed timeline of him just having left the Halloween Party with Nao-chan mere minutes before this conversation between Ayane and Makoto takes place.

So if Selebus now basically came out and outright stated that these are *not* alternate worlds that simply have different starting points in time (which mostly lined up with the explanation given by Himawari in 0.53 of how the Wishing Well works), but, in fact, all actual time states within the same timeline, thus following the rules of causal bullshit that comes with proper time travel, I... have no fucking clue how to even try to decipher what happened during that Halloween party anymore. Why *then*, specifically? What even caused all of that?

Also, does this mean that the Wishing Well canonically allows time travel? So, theoretically, could Akira, like, go back in time and save Sekai from dying, thus "overwriting history" and creating a completely new timeline, where Ami has a mother, Maya never existed and 80% of the shit we know didn't happen?

Time paradoxes sure are fun, Selebus. They sure are...

“All Around the Mulberry Bush” continues directly from the previous event, “Transpacific Sadness Symposium IV: TALKATIVE OBLONG MIRROR”, with Makoto reappearing back in the “real” Halloween Party – which the narrator calls “going to her real home” – seemingly right after Sensei has left with Nao-chan at the end of “Even Gods Get Lost”.

Still having all of the memories of what just happened: both the alternative timeline and her subsequent experience in the Transpacific Sadness Symposium – Makoto immediately tries to contact Sensei via her phone, but fails, as the call doesn’t go through. The girl then notices Ami and Maya, both of whom have also only just arrived to the party (and neither acting strangely in any way, implying that this is happening before Maya is sent to the other world), and tries to reach him via Ami’s phone instead – an attempt that also ultimately ends in complete failure.

spoilers.title: The clustefuck itself
spoilers.html:
Now, this is the part where things get very confusing, very fast:

To begin with, the fact that Makoto’s reappearance chronologically happens at the very end of the party, just after Sensei left, is incredibly strange in and of itself, as, with the exception of possible time lag/fuckery between different alternative worlds, we have no idea when she actually got sent to the other timeline in the first place. The only prior event that prominently features her is “Action/Inaction” in the very beginning of the event chain, and she can also briefly be seen next to Chika in the background of “Empty Heart Appeal”, when Sensei just arrives to the party. Other than that, however, Makoto is almost completely absent from any of the story scenes, and only returns to the spotlight in “Restart”, after the switch has already happened.

Even more importantly, however, the call made by Makoto via Ami’s phone is almost certainly the exact same call Sensei receives in the very beginning of “A House Near a Lake (The Same Place as Always)”, which brings the entire timeline of events of this Halloween Party into question:

The original order of events initially seemed to be:

“Sensei goes with Nao to the School” (“Even Gods Get Lost” / “A House Near A Lake”) -> “Sensei talks to Kaori/Pareidolia on the roof” (“Friend”) -> “Sensei has sex with Kaori after Pareidolia gets deleted” (“Kittens”) -> “SENSEI-QUEST” -> “The Orb/GOD consuming everything” (“Restart”) -> “Alternative world shenanigans” (“Recap”, and all the following events).

Yet “All Around the Mulberry Bush” happens after everything they have experienced in the “Sekai is alive” timeline, even though the call itself happens before “SENSEI-QUEST” and “Restart”.

spoilers.title: Infinite questions
spoilers.html:
So, what does this mean, exactly? Is this a different call and the event itself is a misdirection that is intentionally meant to confuse you, or did Makoto actually time-travel into the past using the “all changes that happen because of time travel have already happened and are accounted for, so you simply play them out as it has already happened” time-travel rules?

And if it’s the latter, what originally happened to Makoto during that Halloween party? Was (is?) there a version of her that actually got to experience the party before being transported into an alternative reality with Sensei, or did she always have her “consciousness replaced” by a future-version of her, that then acted out the events leading up to “SENSEI-QUEST” and then-then had her memories erased before being transported, thus “closing” the loop?

Or is this not the “original” reality, but a different one that is simply very close to it? Meaning that Makoto didn’t “go back in time”, but simply “switched lines” with the foreknowledge of what is going to happen next (thanks to her own timeline). But if so, then what the fuck was with the original phone call Sensei got in “Even the Gods Get Lost”? Was that actually Ami calling him that time?

spoilers.title: Some additional confusing details
spoilers.html:
Also, when Makoto realizes that both of her attempts to reach Sensei have ended in failure and that she has no other alternatives, the girl decides to do the next best thing and go talk to Ayane instead, to see whether she has experienced anything similar. To her dismay, Ayane also reacts with surprise and confusion when confronted with this revelation, which seems to imply that this version of Ayane is yet to experience the timeline switch and only going to go through it at some point in the near future – except for the fact that when the switch does happen, she never once mentions Makoto warning her about it, which either doesn’t mean anything or is a whole other can of worms that only complicates the timeline fuckery even further.

It is also notable that during the same conversation Makoto specifically points that it was *their* Sensei that she met in the other worldline (confirmed by the fact that in his inner narration he repeatedly mentions Pareidolia being gone, implying that this Sensei did indeed go through the events of “Friend”, “Kittens” and “SENSEI-QUEST”), which once again contradicts the supposed timeline of him just having left the Halloween Party with Nao-chan mere minutes before this conversation between Ayane and Makoto takes place.

Thanks for the help everyone.
I'll probably take a look into the puzzle guide when the time comes (I've not got to anything I'd consider a puzzle yet), as for URM I guess it wouldn't hurt to have it installed.

One thing I really don’t get, though, is how seriously I’m supposed to be taking this game. There’s a fairly realistic depiction of high school bullying, one of the main cast members seems to have some kind of body image issue, and then there’s whatever the fuck happened on the “other side of town” with Yumi — but then it suddenly pivots to a character murdering a janitor with a fastball special.
From what little I knew about the game, I went into it expecting a slightly pretentious VN that was meant to be a satire of the genre, which it kind of is. But the tonal whiplash is pretty disorienting.

The other thing I wanted to ask — just to see if I’m on the right track — is about the flower motifs. Some of the girls seem to be associated with specific flowers. Ami has the sunflower from the Chapter 1 icon, and it also shows up during a few of the drug trips / simulation breakdown / “receiving divine knowledge” moments (I think they’re called “Happy events” in-game). Futaba has lavender, which ties into her colour scheme and perfume. Sana has roses from her floor mat, and the sailor girl has a daisy on her pin.
Am I onto something here, or is it just a stylistic choice?

CharlotteWiltshire26 said:
Now, this is the part where things get very confusing, very fast:

To begin with, the fact that Makoto’s reappearance chronologically happens at the very end of the party, just after Sensei left, is incredibly strange in and of itself, as, with the exception of possible time lag/fuckery between different alternative worlds, we have no idea when she actually got sent to the other timeline in the first place. The only prior event that prominently features her is “Action/Inaction” in the very beginning of the event chain, and she can also briefly be seen next to Chika in the background of “Empty Heart Appeal”, when Sensei just arrives to the party. Other than that, however, Makoto is almost completely absent from any of the story scenes, and only returns to the spotlight in “Restart”, after the switch has already happened.

Even more importantly, however, the call made by Makoto via Ami’s phone is almost certainly the exact same call Sensei receives in the very beginning of “A House Near a Lake (The Same Place as Always)”, which brings the entire timeline of events of this Halloween Party into question:

The original order of events initially seemed to be:

“Sensei goes with Nao to the School” (“Even Gods Get Lost” / “A House Near A Lake”) -> “Sensei talks to Kaori/Pareidolia on the roof” (“Friend”) -> “Sensei has sex with Kaori after Pareidolia gets deleted” (“Kittens”) -> “SENSEI-QUEST” -> “The Orb/GOD consuming everything” (“Restart”) -> “Alternative world shenanigans” (“Recap”, and all the following events).

Yet “All Around the Mulberry Bush” happens after everything they have experienced in the “Sekai is alive” timeline, even though the call itself happens before “SENSEI-QUEST” and “Restart”.
Click to expand...

Sel then immediately mentioned the Bootstrap Paradox, a classic trope in science fiction like Interstellar, Triangle, and more recently, the story of WuWa 3.1 and the anime Cosmic Princess Kaguya. Makoto's experience, which you mentioned, is actually a complete closed loop. In the Bootstrap Paradox, there's no need to worry about the beginning or end, you only need to focus on whether each link connects.
Makoto's Bootstrap Paradox is fine, but Himawari sending the scarf back to the past, which I mentioned last time, is another matter. Because Himawari is an external element and not in the loop the entire time, it doesn't seem to fit the Bootstrap Paradox in my opinion. When Sel said that, I was completely certain the scarf incident was over. However, I'm no longer dwelling on it. Sel has his own unique understanding of time.

Both

At least one of the girls with Maya's body type refers to herself as a loli. You can fuck her by the time you reach current update.

I would tell you to join Chinami in the bath in Chapter 2, do it again in Chapter 4 and pick Tsukasa when given the choice in chapter 4. Making lots of saves is also a useful thing in this game. There's a save numbering mod in the OP that I would also recommend now that I think about it. I think there's also a way to handle saves with URM but I never bothered learning.

Ah Sel...he and I have the same music tastes, cause I did IMMEDIATELY recognize those song titles.

The Most Beautiful Bitter Fruit and You And I In Unison are songs by a VERY Emo Band called La Dispute, off of their Album Wildfire.

La Dispute lyric breakdown:


On it's surface, The Most Beautiful Bitter Fruit is about a young teen discovering their sexuality, but if you dive into the lyrics, you find that it's much more about the feelings behind the sexuality. Who am I when I feel desire, am I hesitant or someone that acts, is "restraint integrity, or is it fear"(Which knowing Sara's current events, I think is a BIG DEAL). Part of it, which fits into You And I In Unison, is during the bridge shift, which pushes the song into romantic myth making.

It asks the question whether the relationship was as good as they thought, or have they mythologized the idea of it. There is a massive disparity throughout the song, between body and spirit. The body still wants it, but the mind/spirit is questioning. Elements of jealousy, imagined betrayals, etc.

Standout Lyric:

“What I haven’t done… and what I fear you have
Becomes reality here”

You And I In Unison, however, is about the loss of someone(Sara, so we know about her son), and how that loss shaped them in a significant or meaningful way. Less "I Miss You" and more "I am constructed from your absence"

Quite literally, this song is about how some people don’t just pass through your life, they permanently alter the structure of who you are. While the singer does their best not to place them on a pedestal, they instead place them on a balcony(Literally, it's mentioned in the song), as a balcony is reachable if you climb. This is a song about accepting that some ghosts never leave and deciding that maybe they’re not meant to.



Knowing what we all know about Sara's background, they fit her story very well. I'm really interested in seeing where Sel takes both events, knowing La Dispute the way I do. There is ALOT of fan discourse over these two songs, as the album was their second release and while different from their first, was actually taken to very well by their fans.

posts.content_html_raw:
A new update is nearly upon us, and you know what that means: it's time for me to hastily throw together a post about the last one before everyone has moved on. Let's talk about the main heroine true protagonist of Lessons in Love, Ami Arakawa.

Earlier this month there was a discussion about Sensei questioning whether Ami is really is daughter, and how that might relate to subconscious memories of Himawari. I want to point out that this started before 0.53 - the initial doubts had nothing to do with Himawari.
For reference, here's his latest doubts about Ami's identity:
He had similar doubts after the Nakayarakawayama beach trip, which happened before he learned that Himawari is his daughter.
So I don't think he's rejecting her in favor of his "real" daughter Himawari. I think he's rejecting her in favor of the Ami he remembers from earlier in the game. That's consistent with how other characters have been reacting to her as well. Examples from this update:

(There are more/better examples from earlier - especially with Ayane - but I don't have the references handy.)
Even Ami suggested that she could be a fake. This is presented as a hypothetical, but I still think it plays into the foreshadowing.
Ami would like us to believe she's some secret genius who is expertly "playing the game", but I don't think that's borne out in her actual actions. Since revealing herself as Evil Ami, she has acted on impulse and seems to continually change her mind.
Evil Ami chose to reveal herself to Maya after the seventh reset. If she had pretended not to remember the rape, Maya would have chalked it up as just one more nightmare and not really Ami. Instead, she decided to turn Maya into her toy. This was purely for sadistic pleasure, because as far as I can tell she's gotten zero practical benefit from it.

It certainly wasn't about keeping Maya in line, because Ami encourages her to talk to Sensei and Ayane about Maya Prime and the world. On the other hand, Ami threatens her with death if she reveals Evil Ami's existence to either of them.
But then at Christmalloween, Ayane asks Ami if she knows about the resets - and Ami just casually tells her that she does. It would have been super easy for her to play dumb here. When people have tried to talk to her about similar stuff in the past, she's always faked getting caught in a loop.
Again, Evil Ami accompanies her reveal with a death threat: under no circumstances can Sensei know about her. It's (supposedly) for his own good.

Which brings us to the last update. Evil Ami yet again makes a spur-of-the-moment decision to reveal herself, this time to Sensei. First she shows herself as a rapist, and then when her plan doesn't immediately work, she basically tells him she knows all about the world.
So that's twice now that Evil Ami threatened death if someone found out about her, then she casually revealed herself to the person in question anyway. Neither time was it part of some plan - she reveals herself to Ayane in response to being asked, and she reveals herself to Sensei because Karin happened to show up at her house, giving her an opportunity which was apparently too good to pass up. What happened to her objections to letting Sensei know about her?

What's more, none of this is consistent with Ami's behavior up to the seventh reset and especially before the start of the game. According to her own story, she managed to keep her existence hidden from Maya Prime for millenia (Maya saw her kill people but thought that happened when different Amis broke, rather than a single Ami who stuck around). And now, in the space of a year, she gets so impatient that she starts carelessly revealing herself to everyone? It doesn't seem like the same person is making the decisions.
Ami's reference to the collection is interesting because it reveals 1. she knows about the Collector, and 2. her priorities have shifted. It's also yet another link between her and Pareidolia/USER3.
At the start of Chapter 4, Pareidolia told Sensei he was supposed to become the Collector by fucking all of the girls.
Shortly after that, Ami also mentioned a collection, but I've always been a bit skeptical that she wanted the same thing.
At that point she showed no other sign of wanting him to pursue other girls. She says this is in the same speech:
And when Sensei finally becomes lucid again, she directly contradicts what Pareidolia said about sharing his "love".
So I've tended to believe that either Ami meant a different sort of collection (and one he hadn't started yet) or that he only hallucinated her saying that - the next scene is full of similar blurring of reality.

But now Ami does genuinely want him to become the Collector by fucking all the other girls. This is another change in her that seems to coincide with the seventh reset - leading up to the reset she started broaching the idea of threesomes (with Ayane and Maya), but that was just her latest plan to entice him away from everyone else.
That wasn't the only direct reference to Pareidolia in her meltdown; she also used a specific turn of phrase in exactly the same way Pareidolia used to.

(Arguably this is non-canon because she only says it on the Good Uncle path, but I think it's a valid clue either way)
And here is Pareidolia:

A second time he said it ("Level One"), for good measure:
Pareidolia called Sensei a baby-back bitch to try to goad him into fucking Karin shortly before he almost raped her. Ami calls Sensei a baby-back bitch to goad him when he resists her plan to rape Karin. The parallel is obvious, and it's probably intentional from Ami - she somehow knows exactly what happened in the Karaoke booth.
Only Sensei, Karin, and (partially) Kirin know what happened in that room, and none of them would have told her. But Pareidolia and/or Ghost Sekai might have.
The connections between Ami's Chapter 4 arc and Pareidolia/USER3 keep adding up. Here's a recap:
At the start of Chapter 4, Ami was hearing the voice of at least one God - and one that seems to get on her nerves, like Pareidolia with Sensei.

During last year's Christmas party, there were signs that Ami was being influenced by "Malvin", who represents Pareidolia/USER3.

During the last reset, the happy event showed Ami taken prisoner by a group of spiders. Spiders are the primary symbol of USER3.

Now Ami is buying into USER3's Collector plan and directly quoting language he used when trying to get Sensei to rape Karin.

So whatever is going on with Ami, Pareidolia/USER3 definitely has a hand in it. At best, he's heavily influenced her thinking. At worst, he's exerting some degree of direct control over her.
I have some more thoughts on Ami's relationship with God(s), but I'm going to have to stop here and save those for another post. Maybe I can find time for that tomorrow (don't count on it).

spoilers.title: Ami's erratic behavior
spoilers.html:
Evil Ami chose to reveal herself to Maya after the seventh reset. If she had pretended not to remember the rape, Maya would have chalked it up as just one more nightmare and not really Ami. Instead, she decided to turn Maya into her toy. This was purely for sadistic pleasure, because as far as I can tell she's gotten zero practical benefit from it.

It certainly wasn't about keeping Maya in line, because Ami encourages her to talk to Sensei and Ayane about Maya Prime and the world. On the other hand, Ami threatens her with death if she reveals Evil Ami's existence to either of them.
View attachment 5760993 View attachment 5760994
But then at Christmalloween, Ayane asks Ami if she knows about the resets - and Ami just casually tells her that she does. It would have been super easy for her to play dumb here. When people have tried to talk to her about similar stuff in the past, she's always faked getting caught in a loop.
View attachment 5760995 View attachment 5760997
Again, Evil Ami accompanies her reveal with a death threat: under no circumstances can Sensei know about her. It's (supposedly) for his own good.
View attachment 5761052
View attachment 5761001
Which brings us to the last update. Evil Ami yet again makes a spur-of-the-moment decision to reveal herself, this time to Sensei. First she shows herself as a rapist, and then when her plan doesn't immediately work, she basically tells him she knows all about the world.
View attachment 5761007 View attachment 5761009 View attachment 5761055
So that's twice now that Evil Ami threatened death if someone found out about her, then she casually revealed herself to the person in question anyway. Neither time was it part of some plan - she reveals herself to Ayane in response to being asked, and she reveals herself to Sensei because Karin happened to show up at her house, giving her an opportunity which was apparently too good to pass up. What happened to her objections to letting Sensei know about her?

What's more, none of this is consistent with Ami's behavior up to the seventh reset and especially before the start of the game. According to her own story, she managed to keep her existence hidden from Maya Prime for millenia (Maya saw her kill people but thought that happened when different Amis broke, rather than a single Ami who stuck around). And now, in the space of a year, she gets so impatient that she starts carelessly revealing herself to everyone? It doesn't seem like the same person is making the decisions.

posts.content_html_raw:
Ha ah! I'm back!

Hmm... yeah, my motherboard burned out, so I had to change my PC... now I've gone from a Pentium 3 processor to... the equivalent of a Commodore 64.

Watch out! My 256 MB of RAM will out-fight Skynet's power!
Joke aside, at least I can write my nonsense and give my «review/analysis» of the latest update.

There will be fewer images and more text, because as you can imagine, even if I'm organized (I name and prep everything in advance), it's a nightmare to play with images on a black screen with white text.

So, let's get ready to stumble :

Well... where to start...

Wakana? Let's go for Wakana.

Honestly, her relationship with Sensei is great. Really.

It makes me sad to the highest point to know that she will inevitably join the harem and, thus, lose a large part of her charm.

Also, the scene in the office, with the two clumsy girls with failing chromosomes, made me blow a fuse.
I mean... in what language does Wakana have to express her desire to be calm in a teacher's office when the teacher's absent?!
No, but really, the IQ of those two idiots is ridiculously low!

And especially, for what purpose? Just to express that she has romantic feelings for Sensei...
Frankly, Selebus... go fuck yourself.

I'll skip Noriko's case, because I'm not giving a damn about the lady's little bits.

But to keep with the rosy hair, let's talk a bit, but not too much, about Niki.

First :

I don't have music (I turn off music on all my games. Even on Guitar Hero... I know, I'm dumb.), so I'll just tell you that seeing that made me laugh a lot.

But this :

Finally! But really! Finally!
You have no idea how much joy I felt seeing that.

Actually, I didn't catch anything at the moment. It was with Otoha, the next scene, where we see the same image on her phone that I understood what Niki had done.

I'm old, I know.

Anyways, if Selebus keeps it under wraps and does nothing, damn that would be the worst loss ever.

So... uh... Chika is still completely crazy, Chinami just signed her death sentence (yeah, she swapped germs with Nao, what do you think will happen?) so...

Ami?

Ami, then...

She's still as quirky and dangerous (and I thank Sensei for finally act), but...
I'm increasingly doubtful about her.

Her motives are becoming less clear.


Clearly, she knows the game's rules and she play against Himawari.
Why? I don't know... but all that to say that if Ami is, and will remain for a while, in the «threat» box... I'm more and more wondering what her motives are.

Because I really feel that what she wants is what Himawari wants.

To get her family back.
That's it!
We're on February 27, 1:20 am, and I just finished writing everything. Luckily, I write fast.

Also, just before disappearing until the first of March, Ami, the last word?
And in darkness kill them.




The blood effect isn't that great, I know, but I can't remade it for now...
Also, if anyone can tell me what is Ami hairstyle in Koikatsu, that'll help me a lot. Because I did that thing, who work, but it's not the same.

...

*disappears incestuously*

aramaug said:
According to her own story, she managed to keep her existence hidden from Maya Prime for millenia (Maya saw her kill people but thought that happened when different Amis broke, rather than a single Ami who stuck around). And now, in the space of a year, she gets so impatient that she starts carelessly revealing herself to everyone? It doesn't seem like the same person is making the decisions.
Click to expand...
I'm new here so there's a good chance I'm just missing stuff, but is there a reason I don't see people considering the change to be from when Makoto texts Ami about the resets, and Ayane joking about them?

Perhaps this is overcomplicating things, but could it not be the case that Ami's memories get reset along with everyone else when Akira's reset, and are triggered to come back by being reminded of the resets? So, you essentially have a Nu Ami when you get a Nu Akira, and Maya 'Prime' continues, then someone talks about resets to Nu Ami, bringing back previous memories and instantiating Ami Prime. Ami Prime assesses the current world, and once she decides it's suboptimal she kills people leading up to Akira either fully breaking or being killed himself, in order to restart. She can make Maya her toy too, only to be reset and forget about it until being reminded again, with Maya continuing until she is also reset like we see at the end of ch3. Maya resets through a link with Akira, but not alongside Akira, Ami resets alongside Akira, but can have her memories returned after being reminded of the resets. It wouldn't necessarily have to be a complete, immediate takeover by Ami Prime either, just that's the starting point.

In "All For You", we get Maya talking to Ayane about Ami when she learns of the resets. Ayane asks if she gets in the way of reset progress, and Maya says yes but that "it's far more complicated than just that". Then talks about how the only thing preventing Ami from becoming violent is illusion that she lives the perfect life, that Akira is IN love with her, friends always act in her best interests, and that nothing/no-one gets in the way.

In "Right as Rain", Ami says "I just take what I want. If I’m unlucky enough to end up in a world where that doesn’t work out…I take the world away instead". She also talks about how previous Maya's have been in Nu Maya's position, and it starts great but gets bad once Maya starts figuring things out.

So, I can see a throughline here of Ami Prime wanting her perfect world, and once Maya starts getting close enough to start making progress towards helping them break out of it, she forces a full reset. Before it reaches this or any other breaking point, she's fine with people knowing things to a degree, as long as it still fits with her view of what could be her perfect world.


Again, sleep deprived and new to this, so maybe I'm missing something obvious here, just wanted to share my thoughts on something I haven't seen brought up. Also definitely feel like I wanted to add more to this but it's left my mind at this point lol.

Klldarkness said:
If Ami was older than Maya Prime, is there any reason to think that Maya Prime even WAS Maya Prime?

If a Loop Aware Maya(LAM for short) appears at random, and over thousands of loops becomes the version we interact with for the first few chapters, what's to say she is the original LAM in the first place?
Click to expand...
I'm pretty sure that this was already one of the main takeaways from “Right as Rain”, no?

Specifically, the idea that the Maya we met in Chapter 1 had already been Reset many, many times prior to what happened at the end of Chapter 3, and that her general development within Terminal 23 seemingly follows the cycle of:

Being Reset and losing her memories -> slowly starting to realize that she is stuck in a time loop -> (mistakenly) assuming that she is “Maya Prime” and attempting to escape the loops, either with or without Sensei’s help (though mostly without, as he is extremely fucking useless and also consistently gets Reset every few cycles) -> living through countless instances of the same school year without making any real progress and growing increasingly passive, nihilistic and jaded because of this -> eventually losing all of her memories again -> repeat ad infinitum.

What’s more, I always found it extremely suspicious that, to my knowledge, Maya *never* mentions the actual beginning of the Resets, or references *anything* from her earliest days in the time loop, period. You would think that “the beginning of when everything went to shit” would be an incredibly important point to try to look for answers and potentially discuss among the members of the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad (ESPECIALLY after Ayane joins in), yet it somehow doesn’t come up *even once* throughout the first three Chapters, and after that it’s obviously too late.

There is something deeply unnatural about the fact that Maya appears to be easily able to remember things from before the Resets (like all of her history with Akira, Noriko and Niki) and can mostly remember things well into the Resets (basically from the point where she became the “Maya Prime” we knew), but when it comes to what happened between those two points it’s just… blank. No info, no mentions – no nothing.

This, to me, is very heavily reminiscent of how Maya’s memories of everything prior to meeting Akira work: she can’t really remember her parents, or her birthplace, or her childhood (because there is nothing *to* remember), yet there is a “mental block” of sorts in place to stop the girl from properly dwelling on this and subsequently experiencing an existential crisis from realizing that she doesn’t know basically anything about her own past. Thus, I believe that it’s likely that there is a similar “mental block” on all of her memories concerning the beginning of the loops, which prevents Maya from easily finding out that she is not actually “Maya Prime”.

Finally, the aforementioned cycle of “forgetting, then remembering, then forgetting again” also *technically* appears to be the case for Ami, as well, except that Ami has somehow managed to, for the lack of a better term, “create a cloud backup” of her original consciousness, and so for her it’s just a matter of finding (or orchestrating) a way to “synchronize with the cloud” – after which “Ami Prime” returns – whereas Maya and Akira are effectively forced to start from zero every single time, losing all of their previously gained knowledge. If that is correct, then it’s no wonder why Ami seems to be so much more “aware” of everything compared to everyone else with meta-knowledge (Himawari included), and why she considers herself to be “the true protagonist of this story”.

This, to me, is very heavily reminiscent of how Maya’s memories of everything prior to meeting Akira work: she can’t really remember her parents, or her birthplace, or her childhood (because there is nothing *to* remember), yet there is a “mental block” of sorts in place to stop the girl from properly dwelling on this and subsequently experiencing an existential crisis from realizing that she doesn’t know basically anything about her own past. Thus, I believe that it’s likely that there is a similar “mental block” on all of her memories concerning the beginning of the loops, which prevents Maya from easily finding out that she is not actually “Maya Prime”.

spoilers.title: Some additional thoughts
spoilers.html: Finally, the aforementioned cycle of “forgetting, then remembering, then forgetting again” also *technically* appears to be the case for Ami, as well, except that Ami has somehow managed to, for the lack of a better term, “create a cloud backup” of her original consciousness, and so for her it’s just a matter of finding (or orchestrating) a way to “synchronize with the cloud” – after which “Ami Prime” returns – whereas Maya and Akira are effectively forced to start from zero every single time, losing all of their previously gained knowledge. If that is correct, then it’s no wonder why Ami seems to be so much more “aware” of everything compared to everyone else with meta-knowledge (Himawari included), and why she considers herself to be “the true protagonist of this story”.
