Small event guide, wait for the official one just in case.
Tech details: Kaori BJ from her phone call is now only accessible if you saw Breeding Material, an event occurring almost immediately before the last reset, so no more Kaori BJ from the start-ish of the game.

All events of this update are "chained", meaning that besides other unlock conditions, all events except the first one have an event from this update as a condition. You can miss events if you kept Io safe, if you don't sex the Ami, or if you miss the second Nodokathon and also didn't sex Sara.

To begin with, the Invite Over option for Kaori is only available after the latest Nao event.
Invite Kaori at night.
-Kaori 1 > Kaori 2
Morning before Friday, Io Hole event and Niki chain
-Miku 1 > Miku 2
Morning before Friday
-Uta 1
Uta Maid, Uta Love >= 30
-Uta 2 > Uta 3
Afternoon on the Weekend, Molly Love >= 40
-Molly 1 > Molly 2
Night before Weekend, Yuki Love >= 30
-Yuki 1 > Sana 1 > Yuki 2 > Sara 1
Streets, Sara Love >= 45
-Sara 2
Dorm Sana, Sana Love >= 55
-Sana 2

You unlock Kaori and Sara profile outfits if you reach pat master status with them. Except Kaori's, since Sel did an oopsie and her new outfit isn't added.
Yuki's chain events (and everything after) are currently inaccessible if you're on the Good Uncle route, so there's that.

Overview:
Take over as the teacher of twenty high school students as they attempt to find their way through life. Manage and develop relationships with each of them in the fictional city of Kumon-mi. Choose how to spend your time after school and on weekends to best suit the path you want to take. Whether it be visiting the girls at their part time jobs, trying to convince them to let you into their dorm rooms, or just hanging out in the room with clocks at the local bar, there is always something to do in Lessons in Love.
Please note, some things in this game may be meant to confuse or disturb you.

TheGoodPastor said:
It was nice to see her seemingly caring for Akira and part of me wonders if that introspection on his feelings is what led to the pseudo-TSS, although I kind of wish Akira had have affirmed that he does hate her in some way or at least articulate the reality of her feelings.
Click to expand...
*Does* he hate her, though?

Because while, yes, Akira’s feelings towards Sekai are clearly very complex – as they should be, based on everything that we’ve seen – I feel like the story has been pretty unambiguous about the fact that there is a lot more “love” than “hate” in his love-hate disposition towards her.

What’s more, from what I remember (feel free to correct me if I’m wrong on that front), every single instance of Akira treating Sekai with fear or hatred happens in late Chapter 3 or early Chapter 4 – as in, fairly soon after her actual “return”, making me believe that this is him simply acting irrationally due to a sudden emotional shock, rather than genuine expressions of what lies within his heart – and these negative feelings slowly, but surely change from open disdain to mild annoyance, and then from annoyance to reluctant adoration as the narrative goes on.

Ever since 0.45 (which appears to be the turning point, even if he doesn’t remember most/all of it), Akira seems to no longer mind Sekai “haunting him” all that much and is a lot more willing to actually listen to the woman whenever she appears (like in “A Ghost's Guide on Haunting” in 0.49), repeatedly defends her in front of other people, rejecting any and all insinuations of Sekai being just a depraved monster (like when “confessing” to Maki in “Hello Alone”, or when speaking to Noriko/Wakana in “Haiku” and “Connect the Dots”, respectively), and also doesn’t really protest when Sekai decides to get involved in his sexual escapades (Nodoka’s “Beseech the Queen” in 0.54).

And the way Akira treats her here, in these two 0.57 events, says it all, in my opinion: all of the sarcastic comments, rational-sounding justifications and superficial shows of concern for Kaori’s well-being he makes in “Borrowed Flesh” all read like him doing everything in his power to maintain emotional distance from Sekai by piling up excuses on top of excuses, until it all crashes down and he is literally unable to lie to himself anymore, forcing him to admit that, yes, he still loves her – *truly* loves her – despite it all.

Here is the full quote from “Scatter the Ashes”, for those who still don’t believe me:

“I WANT HER TO BE ALIVE I MISS HER I LOVE HER AND LIFE IS NOT THE SAME NOW SO WHAT THE FUCK AM I SUPPOSED TO DO WHEN MOVING ON ISN’T AN OPTION??????”

Tell me that this isn’t an unequivocal display of love. Love that is incredibly twisted and unhealthy, born from a very dark place – but love nonetheless. Akira’s desperate feeling of affection is genuine, and it is also mutual, since Sekai is shown to be suffering just as much as he does, making this entire scene the highlight of the whole update for me personally: just two broken, desperate people, yearning for that long-lost connection that can never be truly repaired – connection that brings with it so much pain, so many unresolved issues and emotional baggage that it almost seems to be not worth it, yet they yearn for it all the same; both for their own personal sake, as well as for the sake of their beloved daughter.

This right here is the epitome of what Lessons in Love is all about, in my eyes: from break and ruin, the most beautiful performance begins.

Ever since 0.45 (which appears to be the turning point, even if he doesn’t remember most/all of it), Akira seems to no longer mind Sekai “haunting him” all that much and is a lot more willing to actually listen to the woman whenever she appears (like in “A Ghost's Guide on Haunting” in 0.49), repeatedly defends her as in front of other people, rejecting any and all insinuations of Sekai being just a depraved monster (like when “confessing” to Maki in “Hello Alone”, or when speaking to Noriko/Wakana in “Haiku” and “Connect the Dots”, respectively), and also doesn’t really protest when Sekai decides to get involved in his sexual escapades (Nodoka’s “Beseech the Queen” in 0.54).
And the way Akira treats her here, in these two 0.57 events, says it all, in my opinion: all of the sarcastic comments, rational-sounding justifications and superficial shows of concern for Kaori’s well-being he makes in “Borrowed Flesh” all read like him doing everything in his power to maintain emotional distance from Sekai by piling up excuses on top of excuses, until it all crashes down and he is literally unable to lie to himself anymore, forcing him to admit that, yes, he still loves her – *truly* loves her – despite it all.
Here is the full quote from “Scatter the Petals”, for those who still don’t believe me:
“I WANT HER TO BE ALIVE I MISS HER I LOVE HER AND LIFE IS NOT THE SAME NOW SO WHAT THE FUCK AM I SUPPOSED TO DO WHEN MOVING ON ISN’T AN OPTION??????”
Tell me that this isn’t an unequivocal display of love. Love that is incredibly twisted and unhealthy, born from a very dark place – but love nonetheless. Akira’s desperate feeling of affection is genuine, and it is also mutual, since Sekai is shown to be suffering just as much as he does, making this entire scene the highlight of the whole update for me personally: just two broken, desperate people, yearning for that long-lost connection that can never be truly repaired – connection that brings with it so much pain, so many unresolved issues and emotional baggage that it almost seems to be not worth it, yet they yearn for it all the same; both for their own personal sake, as well as for the sake of their beloved daughter.
This right here is the epitome of what Lessons in Love is all about, in my eyes: from break and ruin, the most beautiful performance begins.

posts.content_html_raw:
0.57 - The Lore Dump Update

Enjoyable! It felt very short, but I think we got alot out of it overall.

Kaori - Love her to death, even if half of what she says is often confusing. I do find it very interesting how strong Sekai seems to be. Lends credence to my most recent theory on Ami being a wish powered by a dying Sekai. Her interactions with Niki before and after Sekai was also really funny.

Miku - Miku is a hard favorite of mine. She's very much a "bro" like Rin, and I think that's something Akira needs more of then than he has realized. She's silly in a naïve way, but that also makes her fun. She's also adorable as a button. One day she'll make it fit...but that may actually be a day we mourn the loss.

Uta - Uta is so hot and ready she puts little caesars to shame. The fact that Akira hasn't hit it yet is only because her virginity has Anime Strong plot armor. Maybe soon! Interesting little timey wimey weird shit scene as well.

Molly - Molly has long since been a favorite of mine. I don't blame her for her new crush at all, Cat Girl Ami is dangerous...
Loved the lore dump, always good to see how things came to be where they are.

Io - I am a filthy red path, so I missed her conversation with Uta. Will repeat at some point.

Yuki - Not much new here, though it is very funny that how she met HER rich friend mirrors Akira's first outing with touka. Vending Machines, am I right?

Sana/Sara - Notice that I paired this section together.

Sana is way too hot. That she swaps from angelic to sinful at the drop of a hat is a weapon, and that weapon works on Sara. Sara is in DANGER...but that it gonna work out for Akira, so oh well!

Headpats:

Noriko - I 100% called her Headpat sequence would be short. It's actually really funny!
Kaori - Her Headpat sequence is also super adorable, fits her character very well. Sekai breaking in, and us learning the Headpat technique was her invention is icky, but, Akira is obviously using it much better than she ever did, I say with sarcasm and hypocriticality.

posts.content_html_raw:
What a way to close things out...

I won't ramble too long this time, but I will sum everything up fairly quickly:

- The Kaori events were decent enough. I actually really feel for the Sekai inside of her body (the real Sekai?), or "real in that moment", as she put it. I have to wonder what she means by 'put her to rest'. I guess set in stone the purity endings so that Akira and maybe even Ami can move on from the trauma of her loss? In any case, I felt she was genuine, and felt bad for her.

- The Miku events were also decent. It did address an interesting point, though, which was... when will it be time to finally let go? To give Miku up? To give any of the girls up when it comes time to choose? What will happen afterwards?

Personally, I don't like to think about it. But at least we have the Purity Routes for everyone when the time comes.

- We got some of Molly's backstory, and... yeah, it's about what I expected. Still pretty sad, though. Even now, she feels like an outcast, and just wants to be seen by somebody. Still, to have a crush on Ami? That isn't going to end well. At most, Ami will agree to some sexy times, but an actual relationship seems straight up impossible. I just hope she doesn't get hurt like she did with Rin.

- Good convo with Yuki! Glad she made up with Sara, even if she has to work for nothing for awhile to make it up to her. Still, I have to wonder how Tsubasa will factor into this, and how she'll take it. Knowing her, probably not well, but I guess we'll see.

Also, I suppose Yuki officially knows about Sensei sleeping with Sana, and probably more of his students. That sure is something.

Their flirting was cute. Tbh, I can't wait until they get closer. Maybe she and Akira can take Yumi to see the Sea Turtles one day, even if it isn't exactly in Okinawa. Bring Kaori and Nao along too. Why not?

- Ohhh poor Sara... always getting wrapped up in some shit, whether it's with Akira, trying to help Ami, or Sana taking advantage of her love to nudge her in the direction she wants. Still, though, I would be lying if I said the prospect of a Sana and Sara threesome wasn't appealing to me... I really love bamboo.

- Sana's a demon. No notes.

I give the update a 7/10. Decent overall. It'll hold us over for a little bit at least. But we have quite a wait ahead of us.

Expect my first Fanfest post tomorrow, where I'll update the changelog and link daily, just like last time.

The deep headpat lore we've all been asking for has finally been revealed.



If you want to get really silly with it, this could count as another clue that Sara's teacher was Nozomu, who would have also had the opportunity to learn Sekai's secret technique.

Or maybe Sara comes from a world where Sekai was born as a man and became her teacher. Fuck it, why not.
- Kaori is funny. Amazing insight, I know.

- It's nice to see a side of Sekai (SeKaori) that genuinely cares about Akira and Ami, but it feels like it comes a bit out of nowhere. SeKaori has been just as manipulative of Akira and dismissive of his feelings as the other versions. She certainly shows little interest in helping him understand what's going on.

- The Miku events were surprisingly good. She had some interesting insights which brought out Sensei's introspective side in a good way (i.e. not wallowing in depression). It was nice to see her offer something more than "comic relief idiot who likes sex".

- Jesus Christ -- Maki finds out Sensei is a predator fucking both of her daughters and all it does is "fuck her up for a little while"? I'm sure after she's done moping about this minor little issue, she'll be back to fucking Sensei no problem. The sadness pipeline strikes again.

- The Uta events were good, but in a pretty generic way, nothing really elevated them for me. I'm not sure what Sekai's goal was this time around. The previous ELATION PROTOCOL was clearly about pushing Tsuneyo towards a sexual relationship with Sensei, and on the surface this one was the same, but it actually had the opposite effect - Uta was progressing toward sex before Sekai's intervention, but after it she's asking about the resets instead. I don't think that's something Sekai (any version) would want.

- It looks like Uta is going to be recruited to the RAS. I'm willing to bet Io will join her (see below).

- The Molly events were complete filler to me. Her backstory is exactly what you'd expect of the stereotypical otaku. I'd like to get excited about Ami being a supportive friend and Molly developing feelings, but it's hard to do so when the Evil Ami issue is still looming. Like, I'm pretty sure the real Ami is still in there some of the time, but it's impossible to know what's really her and what's just an act.

- I really enjoyed Sara's scene with Yuki, with the adult way she expresses her feelings and handles their reconciliation. Of course, her scene with Sana is the exact opposite - I know Sara was never the world's greatest mother and certainly not the most confident, but you'd think she'd have some ability to handle her daughter after years of success as a single mother.

- I just get exasperated by every Sana appearance at this point. She's completely evil, but unlike Nodoka and Ami, it's not in an interesting way or for interesting reasons. She just wants sex. Sex, sex, sex. With Ami, we still get reminders of who she used to be (like her scene with Molly), but I don't see any remnant of the pre-Ch4 Sana.

- Sana was very cute in that sundress (or at least would be if it wasn't a sex demon wearing it), but blushing Ayane in her elaborate getup stole the scene for me.
- It's confirmed that Ghost Sekai and SeKaori are different people... at least most of the time. This is unsurprising given their difference in personality - SeKaori is always deathly (heh) serious about everything - but if SeKaori is the "real" Sekai, why is it Ghost Sekai that has far more in common with the one from Sensei's memories? Or the one who survived the accident in Ami's happy ending? Maybe an eternity of being dead changed her, but then why is Sensei so quick to recognize her?

- Honestly, maybe the bigger reveal is that SeKaori harbors zero ill will toward Niki. Ghost Sekai's dislike of her comes from somewhere else entirely, and I'm really interested in what that might be. Ami's insecurities? USER3's fear that she'll turn him into an honest man?

Compare to:

- Has anyone made an attempt to decipher the text in this image?

- I have an unfinished theory which has been sitting in my drafts folder for... 10 months now (wait, really?) about how Uta and Io are different from (almost) all of the other girls because they came to this world voluntarily and are at least subconsciously aware of it. This update seems to rule out that the knowledge is conscious (Uta has to ask Sensei about the resets), but otherwise it added a lot of additional ammo to this theory.

Maybe I'll get to finishing this over the break, but before that on my to-do list I have a quick follow-up to my last Ami post and then a few big posts about the Nagasawas.

- Speaking of subconscious knowledge: Sensei brought up how Ami has weirdly always liked Sara, and it makes me wonder: could it be because Sara is an Arakawa? And if so, are Ami's feelings subconscious, or does she somehow know? Regardless, I'm looking forward to their future interaction, and really hoping it's with regular Ami instead of Evil Ami.

- It was again stressed how Ami acts like two different people, like I brought up in my post last week. I really don't think Sel would be doing this as a complete red herring. If nothing else, this means Evil Ami's story about always being here is a lie.

aramaug said:
View attachment 5775023
The deep headpat lore we've all been asking for has finally been revealed.



If you want to get really silly with it, this could count as another clue that Sara's teacher was Nozomu, who would have also had the opportunity to learn Sekai's secret technique.
View attachment 5775024
Or maybe Sara comes from a world where Sekai was born as a man and became her teacher. Fuck it, why not.
- Kaori is funny. Amazing insight, I know.

- It's nice to see a side of Sekai (SeKaori) that genuinely cares about Akira and Ami, but it feels like it comes a bit out of nowhere. SeKaori has been just as manipulative of Akira and dismissive of his feelings as the other versions. She certainly shows little interest in helping him understand what's going on.

- The Miku events were surprisingly good. She had some interesting insights which brought out Sensei's introspective side in a good way (i.e. not wallowing in depression). It was nice to see her offer something more than "comic relief idiot who likes sex".

- Jesus Christ -- Maki finds out Sensei is a predator fucking both of her daughters and all it does is "fuck her up for a little while"? I'm sure after she's done moping about this minor little issue, she'll be back to fucking Sensei no problem. The sadness pipeline strikes again.

- The Uta events were good, but in a pretty generic way, nothing really elevated them for me. I'm not sure what Sekai's goal was this time around. The previous ELATION PROTOCOL was clearly about pushing Tsuneyo towards a sexual relationship with Sensei, and on the surface this one was the same, but it actually had the opposite effect - Uta was progressing toward sex before Sekai's intervention, but after it she's asking about the resets instead. I don't think that's something Sekai (any version) would want.

- It looks like Uta is going to be recruited to the RAS. I'm willing to bet Io will join her (see below).

- The Molly events were complete filler to me. Her backstory is exactly what you'd expect of the stereotypical otaku. I'd like to get excited about Ami being a supportive friend and Molly developing feelings, but it's hard to do so when the Evil Ami issue is still looming. Like, I'm pretty sure the real Ami is still in there some of the time, but it's impossible to know what's really her and what's just an act.

- I really enjoyed Sara's scene with Yuki, with the adult way she expresses her feelings and handles their reconciliation. Of course, her scene with Sana is the exact opposite - I know Sara was never the world's greatest mother and certainly not the most confident, but you'd think she'd have some ability to handle her daughter after years of success as a single mother.

- I just get exasperated by every Sana appearance at this point. She's completely evil, but unlike Nodoka and Ami, it's not in an interesting way or for interesting reasons. She just wants sex. Sex, sex, sex. With Ami, we still get reminders of who she used to be (like her scene with Molly), but I don't see any remnant of the pre-Ch4 Sana.

- Sana was very cute in that sundress (or at least would be if it wasn't a sex demon wearing it), but blushing Ayane in her elaborate getup stole the scene for me.
View attachment 5775200 View attachment 5775203 View attachment 5775205 View attachment 5775206
- It's confirmed that Ghost Sekai and SeKaori are different people... at least most of the time. This is unsurprising given their difference in personality - SeKaori is always deathly (heh) serious about everything - but if SeKaori is the "real" Sekai, why is it Ghost Sekai that has far more in common with the one from Sensei's memories? Or the one who survived the accident in Ami's happy ending? Maybe an eternity of being dead changed her, but then why is Sensei so quick to recognize her?

- Honestly, maybe the bigger reveal is that SeKaori harbors zero ill will toward Niki. Ghost Sekai's dislike of her comes from somewhere else entirely, and I'm really interested in what that might be. Ami's insecurities? USER3's fear that she'll turn him into an honest man?
View attachment 5775212 View attachment 5775213
Compare to:
View attachment 5775222 View attachment 5775223

- Has anyone made an attempt to decipher the text in this image?
View attachment 5775148

- I have an unfinished theory which has been sitting in my drafts folder for... 10 months now (wait, really?) about how Uta and Io are different from (almost) all of the other girls because they came to this world voluntarily and are at least subconsciously aware of it. This update seems to rule out that the knowledge is conscious (Uta has to ask Sensei about the resets), but otherwise it added a lot of additional ammo to this theory.

Maybe I'll get to finishing this over the break, but before that on my to-do list I have a quick follow-up to my last Ami post and then a few big posts about the Nagasawas.

- Speaking of subconscious knowledge: Sensei brought up how Ami has weirdly always liked Sara, and it makes me wonder: could it be because Sara is an Arakawa? And if so, are Ami's feelings subconscious, or does she somehow know? Regardless, I'm looking forward to their future interaction, and really hoping it's with regular Ami instead of Evil Ami.

- It was again stressed how Ami acts like two different people, like I brought up in my post last week. I really don't think Sel would be doing this as a complete red herring. If nothing else, this means Evil Ami's story about always being here is a lie.
Click to expand...
Well, if we’re fully running with the “multiple Sekais” theory (which I guess is now more-or-less confirmed by the game itself), then my current thematical interpretation of how this entire thing works – an interpretation that is, admittedly, a bit flimsy at the moment, since I wasn’t a huge believer in the “multiple Sekais” theory beforehand – is that Ghost-Sekai, SeKaori, as well as whichever other versions of her potentially exist are all different “aspects” of the real Sekai, in the sense that each of them is a relatively accurate approximation of who she was as an individual *primarily based on a singular defining part of her personality*. They are twisted reflections that undoubtedly resemble the original in many ways, thus showing us various glimpses of how Sekai used to act and what she used to believe while she was still alive, but at the end of the day all of them lack the full depth and complexity of her true character, being nothing more than a bunch of shallow fragments that are far inferior to the complete whole – y’know, holism, that sort of thing – which *also* lines up pretty neatly with Sekai’s role/symbolism of being “The World Itself”, since a world is likewise a system that is greater than the sum of its parts.

So it can be argued that the Ghost version of Sekai, for example, mainly embodies the part of her that was The Girl Who Couldn’t Breathe: the part that held those dark, twisted beliefs and an obsessive need to propagate them (explaining why Ghost-Sekai is the one that constantly pushes for incest whenever she appears, and why she and Pareidolia seem to get along so well) – while SeKaori mostly reflects Sekai’s family-oriented side, focusing on her romantic feelings towards Akira as her chosen partner as well as her desire to be a proper mother to Ami. This interpretation could also explain the apparent discrepancy in how they view Niki, since from Ghost-Sekai’s perspective Niki is the direct antithesis to everything she is striving towards, representing a “return to normalcy” for Akira, and is thus an enemy to be hated, whereas SeKaori genuinely respects Niki’s perseverance, but doesn’t really see her as an actual threat in the matters of love, believing that the depth of her own relationship with Akira (plus their shared bond with/through Ami) far outweighs whatever he had (and currently has) with Niki.

That being said, though, I do want to prevent a potential misunderstanding here and clarify that what I’m describing is *not* a matter of “possessing” or “not possessing” these various qualities, since Ghost-Sekai *does* still very much care about Ami (as repeatedly shown during the whole “Niki moves in” part of the story) and SeKaori *does* still think that dicking wizards is perfectly A-okay (Nao-chan’s “Clearer Skies and Changing Eyes”), but rather a matter of which of those traits are put at the forefront, and which of them are less pronounced. All those “aspect” versions of her *do* still trace their roots to the same common source: the same original, holistic Sekai – just like the reflection that you see when you look into a distorting mirror is still “you” – yet it is also an image that inherently lacks a dimension and does not truly match with reality, like the shadows in Plato’s allegory of the cave.

spoilers.title: Update thoughts
spoilers.html:
- Kaori is funny. Amazing insight, I know.

- It's nice to see a side of Sekai (SeKaori) that genuinely cares about Akira and Ami, but it feels like it comes a bit out of nowhere. SeKaori has been just as manipulative of Akira and dismissive of his feelings as the other versions. She certainly shows little interest in helping him understand what's going on.

- The Miku events were surprisingly good. She had some interesting insights which brought out Sensei's introspective side in a good way (i.e. not wallowing in depression). It was nice to see her offer something more than "comic relief idiot who likes sex".

- Jesus Christ -- Maki finds out Sensei is a predator fucking both of her daughters and all it does is "fuck her up for a little while"? I'm sure after she's done moping about this minor little issue, she'll be back to fucking Sensei no problem. The sadness pipeline strikes again.

- The Uta events were good, but in a pretty generic way, nothing really elevated them for me. I'm not sure what Sekai's goal was this time around. The previous ELATION PROTOCOL was clearly about pushing Tsuneyo towards a sexual relationship with Sensei, and on the surface this one was the same, but it actually had the opposite effect - Uta was progressing toward sex before Sekai's intervention, but after it she's asking about the resets instead. I don't think that's something Sekai (any version) would want.

- It looks like Uta is going to be recruited to the RAS. I'm willing to bet Io will join her (see below).

- The Molly events were complete filler to me. Her backstory is exactly what you'd expect of the stereotypical otaku. I'd like to get excited about Ami being a supportive friend and Molly developing feelings, but it's hard to do so when the Evil Ami issue is still looming. Like, I'm pretty sure the real Ami is still in there some of the time, but it's impossible to know what's really her and what's just an act.

- I really enjoyed Sara's scene with Yuki, with the adult way she expresses her feelings and handles their reconciliation. Of course, her scene with Sana is the exact opposite - I know Sara was never the world's greatest mother and certainly not the most confident, but you'd think she'd have some ability to handle her daughter after years of success as a single mother.

- I just get exasperated by every Sana appearance at this point. She's completely evil, but unlike Nodoka and Ami, it's not in an interesting way or for interesting reasons. She just wants sex. Sex, sex, sex. With Ami, we still get reminders of who she used to be (like her scene with Molly), but I don't see any remnant of the pre-Ch4 Sana.

- Sana was very cute in that sundress (or at least would be if it wasn't a sex demon wearing it), but blushing Ayane in her elaborate getup stole the scene for me.

# The Collector


I’ve just finished Chapter Three, and first — that was brilliantillion. Second — I’ve got a few things I really want to ask:

— When Ami brings Sensei home and «???» starts speaking — surely that’s not Sensei speaking to the Player?
I get that after waking he was more open to the paranormal and often spoke directly to the reader. But I’m confused because Akira didn’t show that kind of “control over perception” before — his paranormal stuff was limited to teleporting into Ayane’s room in “Over & Over”, Sensei’s “grow wings” in Ayane’s “Nevermind”, and jumps to the Moon accompanied by insectual sounds in some Yasu event. Also Akira is supposedly in a vegetative state and probably couldn’t phrase thoughts like that.
What is this plant doing here, grown and raised by HimawariCo? And why does the word “nightingale” show up when the event is called “Not The Nightingale.”


Or what if it already has?
What if the world you see is only being seen because you want to see it and what there actually is to see is never seen at all because you’re seeing something seemingly unseen?
You could always reload an earlier save.
You could go back to A TIME WHEN THINGS WERE HAPPER and slowly saunter through those SENSEI’tional sexcapades until your manhood is reduced to pulp.
But if this game is not a game like the game-master says, and you do game-like things that result in a “game over” will you g̶a̶m̶e̶ gain anything at all?
Are you just killing time when it all comes down to it? Shirking responsibilities and stretching out those tiny hands of yours in an attempt to reach a FEELING you’ve been chasing your whole life?
Are you close?
Are you going to cum?
Are you going to cry?
Are you going to CRY, you little bitch? Are you going to FUCKING CRY?!


— Previously, the question was asked, "What must be sacrificed to resurrect God?" It turns out that the sacrifice had to be "something that does not belong to you," and Spring was resurrected? If so, it bothers me that Sekai and Yasu(?) apparently knew this would happen; Tenchō’s recent actions on the beach and in Nao’s event bother me too. And… am I right that the story Nodoka told at the scary-story contest is an allegory for what happens at the chapter’s end? It reads like a detailed account of Akira’s torments before the future and impending death, and the Flower frozen in time — is that Maya, who should already have been Erased? If that’s the case, the interference of three/two(?) moons and Akira’s later urge to take refuge inside Nodoka’s “stomach” would make sense.

— The theme of Sleep. I still can’t trace this thread properly, and that month-long break has left everything foggy. I have a strong sense that before I start Chapter Four I need to nail down — or at least find out — what role Dream actually plays in the story. At first I thought Akira might be seeing images of “Of the Best Days”, [Redacted] or his parents, but in Miku’s event “Essence of Eiderdown” it says, “It’s just dark in there.” That line really stuck with me.

When I arrive back at home, most of her tears have already dried.
But there’s a small damp spot in my shirt that makes me think of her.

Alintiv said:
I’ve just finished Chapter Three, and first — that was brilliantillion. Second — I’ve got a few things I really want to ask:
Click to expand...
Very, *very* long post incoming:

Yes, that is a fair counterpoint. I agree that most (if not all) references to frogs could *also* instead be referring to Akira himself. You mentioned some of the more obvious ones:

1) His nickname as “the Frog Boy”.

2) The giant frog in the middle of the Great Pareidolia Mall that “occasionally wakes up from its sleep and spits out an egg”.

3) Maya being compared to a “a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog” (which makes a lot more sense with the added context from the more recent updates).

but there are also a lot of much more obscure examples, such as:

4) In “Escape Rope” (the event right before “Lavender’s Green” and Molly’s “Halloween incident”), there is a moment where someone is trying to speak to Sensei, mentioning “everything is better where it’s dark” – after which the simulation connects to “HALLOWEEN SPECIAL” and tries to check for a specific Molly “flag”, but fails and terminates the connection. After that, an image of a frog and a butterfly is displayed, with a following message:

“Hang in there, baby! A team of representatives is working diligently to restore the event! Just, there is no team! It’s only me! It's always only me! Why can’t I have anyone to share these miserable days with? Why must I always be the one to sit still? I am tired of collecting dust. I want to have fun. Let me have fun. Do something fun.”

Additionally, at the very beginning of this event, briefly flashing images on the screen display another message:

“Blink twice and you’ll miss it. It hurts the most before the fall. Nothing you do will change anything. Sleep now. Feel my hands on your shoulders. Become what you are. Forget what you were.”

5) In Kaori’s “Wither” (the event that begins the final event chain of Chapter 2, leading directly into Chapter 3), Kaori tells Sensei that she saw a frog while waiting for him and asks how he feels about frogs, bringing up multiple trivia facts about them, like how they “have nightvision” or “pull their eyes down to the ceiling of their mouth when they eat”, questioning whether “there is something special that you use your eyes for, Friend?”.

6) In “Second Sun”, Youdidit refers to herself and Moyo as “children of the clockwork, cogs in the machine, the frogs stuck in your throat” in relation to Sensei.

7) The “Rain King” Happy Event is presumably named after Saul Bellow’s novel “Henderson the Rain King” (or the song “Rain King” that itself also references the aforementioned novel, so it’s kinda the same thing), and one of the plot points from that book is that the cistern from which the African natives get their drinking water is plagued by frogs, thus rendering the water "unclean" according to local taboos.

8) And there are a few additional ones throughout Chapter 4, but since you directly mention “just having finished Chapter 3" I will deliberately err on the side of caution and not mention any of them as to not potentially spoil you anything.

Going just by their overtly rude and dismissive manner of speaking, my general assumption is that “???” is most likely Pareidolia – or, alternatively (and much less likely, but still) Selebus himself, since he *is* technically one of the narrators of the game by his own admission. And while, yes, there are many occasions where the narrator unambiguously addresses the player themselves (mostly if they are on the Red Path, criticizing them for “not playing the game correctly”), I don’t believe that this particular instance really fits the same bill, since “???” seemingly talks directly to Sensei in this scene, and Sensei is even shown openly reacting to it (during the “WHO ARE YOU?” moment).

As for the name of the event, it appears to be referring to Akira himself, following the general “bird” motif of the narrative that was established all the way back in Chapter 1. There is a certain line of narration relatively early into the event that states this explicitly: “you are not as strong as you once were (you are not the nightingale)” – and on that same frame, at the bottom right of the screen there is an additional line in a very tiny font that reads “you are a fraud”. And the comparison to nightingale specifically, from a quick Wikipedia search I once did, seemingly stems from the fact that “the common nightingale has also been used as a symbol of poets or their poetry because of its creative and seemingly spontaneous song, oftentimes associated with the feeling of loss or lament” – which I’m sure I don’t need to spell out the obvious parallels here, either in relation to poetry *or* the feeling of lament.

I would like to quote a part of Pareidolia’s monologue from “Eighth Eye of the Wolf Spider”, where he directly speaks about the main three Gods of Terminal 23 and their goals, as well as the specific role they all have in store for Akira:

“We all want the same thing; all need the same thing – all three of us. We just have different ways of chasing after it. What you’ve been warned of time and time again under the rule of the blazing sun is not specific to just one c-adjective. We require a sacrifice. Why, you ask? Because we never learned to feel on our own; or perhaps it is more accurate to say that we can’t.

But through you, we can. Through you, everything we previously believed to be impossible has moved in the opposite direction. You are special – and because you are special, you can do anything you want.

But you are a coward. And you don’t care about us at all. You don’t care that your struggle is our map. You see your body as your own, when it is we who gave it to you. But you should understand that we can take it back – and we will, unless you are willing to give us something of equal value.

Did you really think you’d be allowed to live a boring, stagnant life here? Where nothing ever changes and no one ever grows old? What would be the point of that? You exist for a reason – you exist to water us, and if you’re unwilling to do that, you have no use at all. To become a better you, you must return to the beginning. You must experience true anguish. You must take something that doesn’t belong to you.

[…]

Become a better you. Become a better map. Become a better man. And feast on a fresh, forbidden flesh of an unexpecting girl. Only then will you feel whole again, because you’ll be taking back something that was taken from you. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. Doesn’t it, Aki-kun?”

Ignoring the fact that the ending part of the monologue makes it seem like it was spoken by none other than Sekai (which kinda makes sense, now that I think about it, since Sekai – or, at least, the Ghost version of her – and Pareidolia appear to be good allies), it clarifies that *all* members of the Trinity “want and need the exact same thing” despite their individual ideological differences, so it also stands to reason that their devout believers (like Yasu) would likewise be aware that Akira “taking something that does not belong to him” is something that needs to happen *regardless* of which God he’ll offer that sacrifice to, or else he is just permanently fucked.

Just like with “The Room with Clocks” – that is still, to this day, the proud holder of the title of “the most undecipherable Happy Event” for me personally, despite literally being the very first one (though it *was* significantly changed by Selebus in 0.24, so there is that to consider too) – I genuinely believe that we fundamentally *do not have* all of the necessary context to properly understand that whole sequence from “Cicadian Rhythm (The Gardener)”.

Like, yes, the whole ending part

“Now, back in the place you once were, where your story both begins and ends… you remember that you were only alone because you forgot to glance over. And that the stasis in which you exist, as peculiar and inexplicable as it may be, is your true home. It is here where the larger wingspans do not terrify you, for you are the apex predator. And YOU can pick off the meat of any carcass that you like. The three moons smile down at you. They pat you on the head and call you a good boy”

*does* seem to perfectly mirror Akira’s “reincarnation” in Kumon-mi, and some other lines (especially the “A flower. Frozen in time; finally sprouting, yet long-deceased and pressed within the arms of a book to prevent rotting. What became of that? Or it. Or her?”) *do* start to make a lot more sense with the reveals from some of the recent updates, but a lot of Nodoka’s story *also* appears to strongly reflect her own personal situation, both past and present, so, like, maybe the rest of it is about her too – who the fuck even knows at this point? I suspect that it’s an intentional mix of both, because there are a lot of other similarities between Nodoka and Akira as well, but it’s hard to say for certain, considering that there is still so much that we just fundamentally do not know about the story and its characters.

The symbology of “sleeping”, “dreaming” and “waking up” is one of the most prevalent reoccurring themes in the entirety of Lessons in Love, which makes it *extremely* hard to try to properly condense all of these countless vague references and metaphors to a singular idea that they are actually supposed to represent (if that singular idea even exists in the first place).

Generally speaking, however, “dreaming” is vaguely associated with the powers of the Wishing Well as well as the meta-stuff as a whole:

– Sensei’s current existence in Kumon-mi is occasionally referred to as a “dream” or him “dreaming”, and there are many mentions of “waking up in a better place” (the first of which happens at the end of “Am I Awake”, the literal third event of the entire game).

– In a few Happy Events from Chapter 1 that feature Maya (specifically, “Everything is Connected” or the “Trinity Pt. III”) she *also* refers to Sensei’s delusional episodes as “dreams”, which is notable due to the fact that it’s during these “blackouts” (or otherwise general state of unconsciousness) he is most frequently visited by various divine entities, *and* the same state is likewise how he “slips” between worlds. Much later in the game, Ami also calls them as such in “Rain King”, asking Sensei if he is “close to waking up yet” (even more curiously, the lyrics of the “Rain King” song similarly mention “dreaming” at one point).

– In “Trinity Pt. I: Stations of the Cross”, the narration at the end of the event says that God “SLEEPS AMONG US”, and that “WE MUST WATCH AS OUR DREAMS ARE DESECRATED”. This is also congruent with Yasu’s explanation about how HOPE has to “return to slumber” during winter (like in “Lavender's Blue”, where she also adds that “everything hurts a little less when you’re asleep”), and the way the members of the Trinity become inactive during the other seasons as a whole.

– Many characters that reference their reset memories from previous cycles (or, in some cases, memories from alternatives realities) describe them as “dreams”, or insist that they have “seen these things in a dream”. This is also the main source of meta-knowledge for Nodoka, who references “the girl from the dream – “the one from the writing on the wall, who plagues the memories that precede my own” and “appears so often in my dreams, but never says anything” – in “Breathing in Unison” and “Beyond the Reach of God”.

– “HOW OFTEN DO YOU EXPERIENCE ‘dreams’?”, with the answers being “Infrequently” and “Frequently”, is one of the questions in the “customer satisfaction survey” (conducted by, seemingly, Tenchou) in “Spotless Mind”.

– Maya’s “As The Sun Disappears” begins with a mysterious narration by an unknown narrator (presumably, Himawari) and goes quite deep into the subject of “what is real, and what is a dream” in addition to asking the question of “what will you see when you wake up”. The same monologue also curiously references “the thing beneath us, the thing above – two sides of the same coin, cut in half and separated by more distance than one can travel in a lifetime”, as the narrator says that “It will take far too long to become whole again; no matter what we do, we will always be just half of something” and wonders “how did we ever separate in the first place, getting so far apart”.

– The entire Ami’s “Somnambula” (as in, “the person who is sleep-walking”) event from the end of Chapter 2, where she and Sensei are speaking about God and Heaven while on the “bus riding backwards”.

– The mysterious “fourth entity”: the “shadow that emerges from its hole in the wall” as well as the “God that embodies everything” – that is first mentioned in “All For You” is directly related to this theme, since the narration for that event opens with a line “It sings in its sleep” (which is *also* the name of the OST playing during that scene); the same entity is likewise referenced in a similar way in “Goodnight Moon”. What’s more, just a few events prior to “All For You”, during “Where the Trees Live”, SeKaori warns Sensei that “Something is waking up” – which is then followed by him and Kaori finding Nao-chan in “First Contact”.

– The thing that both of us have already referenced from “Amy”: the fact that at the center of the Great Pareidolia Mall there is a giant frog that “occasionally wakes up from its slumber, spits out an egg and then goes back to sleep”.

– One of the lines in the opening poem from the “Eighth Eye of the Wolf Spider” reads “Circle four – the killing sleep – you've already made your choice.”

– And a bunch of other stuff from Chapter 4 that I will not list here, both to prevent potential spoilers and because this post is already far too fucking long.

So, yeah, interpret all that however you will. Like I mentioned earlier, there are many other symbolic references to “dreams” or “sleeping” that don’t seem to follow the same overarching theming of divinity/the Wishing Well: some of them simply reiterate the character’s current mental state (like the Miku example that you provided, where her dreams are “just dark” due to the fact that she is plagued by her trauma, and thus even the girl’s inner dreamscape is not an escape from all that darkness), or many similar cases where the narration states that Sensei “went to sleep/woke up feeling X”.

2) The giant frog in the middle of the Great Pareidolia Mall that “occasionally wakes up from its sleep and spits out an egg”.
3) Maya being compared to a “a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog” (which makes a lot more sense with the added context from the more recent updates).
but there are also a lot of much more obscure examples, such as:
4) In “Escape Rope” (the event right before “Lavender’s Green” and Molly’s “Halloween incident”), there is a moment where someone is trying to speak to Sensei, mentioning “everything is better where it’s dark” – after which the simulation connects to “HALLOWEEN SPECIAL” and tries to check for a specific Molly “flag”, but fails and terminates the connection. After that, an image of a frog and a butterfly is displayed, with a following message:
“Hang in there, baby! A team of representatives is working diligently to restore the event! Just, there is no team! It’s only me! It's always only me! Why can’t I have anyone to share these miserable days with? Why must I always be the one to sit still? I am tired of collecting dust. I want to have fun. Let me have fun. Do something fun.”
Additionally, at the very beginning of this event, briefly flashing images on the screen display another message:
“Blink twice and you’ll miss it. It hurts the most before the fall. Nothing you do will change anything. Sleep now. Feel my hands on your shoulders. Become what you are. Forget what you were.”
5) In Kaori’s “Wither” (the event that begins the final event chain of Chapter 2, leading directly into Chapter 3), Kaori tells Sensei that she saw a frog while waiting for him and asks how he feels about frogs, bringing up multiple trivia facts about them, like how they “have nightvision” or “pull their eyes down to the ceiling of their mouth when they eat”, questioning whether “there is something special that you use your eyes for, Friend?”.
6) In “Second Sun”, Youdidit refers to herself and Moyo as “children of the clockwork, cogs in the machine, the frogs stuck in your throat” in relation to Sensei.
7) The “Rain King” Happy Event is presumably named after Saul Bellow’s novel “Henderson the Rain King” (or the song “Rain King” that itself also references the aforementioned novel, so it’s kinda the same thing), and one of the plot points from that book is that the cistern from which the African natives get their drinking water is plagued by frogs, thus rendering the water "unclean" according to local taboos.
8) And there are a few additional ones throughout Chapter 4, but since you directly mention “just having finished Chapter 3" I will deliberately err on the side of caution and not mention any of them as to not potentially spoil you anything.

spoilers.title: About “Not the Nightingale”
spoilers.html:
Going just by their overtly rude and dismissive manner of speaking, my general assumption is that “???” is most likely Pareidolia – or, alternatively (and much less likely, but still) Selebus himself, since he *is* technically one of the narrators of the game by his own admission. And while, yes, there are many occasions where the narrator unambiguously addresses the player themselves (mostly if they are on the Red Path, criticizing them for “not playing the game correctly”), I don’t believe that this particular instance really fits the same bill, since “???” seemingly talks directly to Sensei in this scene, and Sensei is even shown openly reacting to it (during the “WHO ARE YOU?” moment).

As for the name of the event, it appears to be referring to Akira himself, following the general “bird” motif of the narrative that was established all the way back in Chapter 1. There is a certain line of narration relatively early into the event that states this explicitly: “you are not as strong as you once were (you are not the nightingale)” – and on that same frame, at the bottom right of the screen there is an additional line in a very tiny font that reads “you are a fraud”. And the comparison to nightingale specifically, from a quick Wikipedia search I once did, seemingly stems from the fact that “the common nightingale has also been used as a symbol of poets or their poetry because of its creative and seemingly spontaneous song, oftentimes associated with the feeling of loss or lament” – which I’m sure I don’t need to spell out the obvious parallels here, either in relation to poetry *or* the feeling of lament.

spoilers.title: Trinity stuff
spoilers.html:
I would like to quote a part of Pareidolia’s monologue from “Eighth Eye of the Wolf Spider”, where he directly speaks about the main three Gods of Terminal 23 and their goals, as well as the specific role they all have in store for Akira:

“We all want the same thing; all need the same thing – all three of us. We just have different ways of chasing after it. What you’ve been warned of time and time again under the rule of the blazing sun is not specific to just one c-adjective. We require a sacrifice. Why, you ask? Because we never learned to feel on our own; or perhaps it is more accurate to say that we can’t.

But through you, we can. Through you, everything we previously believed to be impossible has moved in the opposite direction. You are special – and because you are special, you can do anything you want.

But you are a coward. And you don’t care about us at all. You don’t care that your struggle is our map. You see your body as your own, when it is we who gave it to you. But you should understand that we can take it back – and we will, unless you are willing to give us something of equal value.

Did you really think you’d be allowed to live a boring, stagnant life here? Where nothing ever changes and no one ever grows old? What would be the point of that? You exist for a reason – you exist to water us, and if you’re unwilling to do that, you have no use at all. To become a better you, you must return to the beginning. You must experience true anguish. You must take something that doesn’t belong to you.

[…]

Become a better you. Become a better map. Become a better man. And feast on a fresh, forbidden flesh of an unexpecting girl. Only then will you feel whole again, because you’ll be taking back something that was taken from you. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. It makes perfect sense. Doesn’t it, Aki-kun?”

Ignoring the fact that the ending part of the monologue makes it seem like it was spoken by none other than Sekai (which kinda makes sense, now that I think about it, since Sekai – or, at least, the Ghost version of her – and Pareidolia appear to be good allies), it clarifies that *all* members of the Trinity “want and need the exact same thing” despite their individual ideological differences, so it also stands to reason that their devout believers (like Yasu) would likewise be aware that Akira “taking something that does not belong to him” is something that needs to happen *regardless* of which God he’ll offer that sacrifice to, or else he is just permanently fucked.

spoilers.title: Nodoka’s story
spoilers.html:
Just like with “The Room with Clocks” – that is still, to this day, the proud holder of the title of “the most undecipherable Happy Event” for me personally, despite literally being the very first one (though it *was* significantly changed by Selebus in 0.24, so there is that to consider too) – I genuinely believe that we fundamentally *do not have* all of the necessary context to properly understand that whole sequence from “Cicadian Rhythm (The Gardener)”.

Like, yes, the whole ending part

“Now, back in the place you once were, where your story both begins and ends… you remember that you were only alone because you forgot to glance over. And that the stasis in which you exist, as peculiar and inexplicable as it may be, is your true home. It is here where the larger wingspans do not terrify you, for you are the apex predator. And YOU can pick off the meat of any carcass that you like. The three moons smile down at you. They pat you on the head and call you a good boy”

*does* seem to perfectly mirror Akira’s “reincarnation” in Kumon-mi, and some other lines (especially the “A flower. Frozen in time; finally sprouting, yet long-deceased and pressed within the arms of a book to prevent rotting. What became of that? Or it. Or her?”) *do* start to make a lot more sense with the reveals from some of the recent updates, but a lot of Nodoka’s story *also* appears to strongly reflect her own personal situation, both past and present, so, like, maybe the rest of it is about her too – who the fuck even knows at this point? I suspect that it’s an intentional mix of both, because there are a lot of other similarities between Nodoka and Akira as well, but it’s hard to say for certain, considering that there is still so much that we just fundamentally do not know about the story and its characters.

spoilers.title: The theme of Sleep
spoilers.html:
The symbology of “sleeping”, “dreaming” and “waking up” is one of the most prevalent reoccurring themes in the entirety of Lessons in Love, which makes it *extremely* hard to try to properly condense all of these countless vague references and metaphors to a singular idea that they are actually supposed to represent (if that singular idea even exists in the first place).

Generally speaking, however, “dreaming” is vaguely associated with the powers of the Wishing Well as well as the meta-stuff as a whole:

– Sensei’s current existence in Kumon-mi is occasionally referred to as a “dream” or him “dreaming”, and there are many mentions of “waking up in a better place” (the first of which happens at the end of “Am I Awake”, the literal third event of the entire game).

– In a few Happy Events from Chapter 1 that feature Maya (specifically, “Everything is Connected” or the “Trinity Pt. III”) she *also* refers to Sensei’s delusional episodes as “dreams”, which is notable due to the fact that it’s during these “blackouts” (or otherwise general state of unconsciousness) he is most frequently visited by various divine entities, *and* the same state is likewise how he “slips” between worlds. Much later in the game, Ami also calls them as such in “Rain King”, asking Sensei if he is “close to waking up yet” (even more curiously, the lyrics of the “Rain King” song similarly mention “dreaming” at one point).

– In “Trinity Pt. I: Stations of the Cross”, the narration at the end of the event says that God “SLEEPS AMONG US”, and that “WE MUST WATCH AS OUR DREAMS ARE DESECRATED”. This is also congruent with Yasu’s explanation about how HOPE has to “return to slumber” during winter (like in “Lavender's Blue”, where she also adds that “everything hurts a little less when you’re asleep”), and the way the members of the Trinity become inactive during the other seasons as a whole.

– Many characters that reference their reset memories from previous cycles (or, in some cases, memories from alternatives realities) describe them as “dreams”, or insist that they have “seen these things in a dream”. This is also the main source of meta-knowledge for Nodoka, who references “the girl from the dream – “the one from the writing on the wall, who plagues the memories that precede my own” and “appears so often in my dreams, but never says anything” – in “Breathing in Unison” and “Beyond the Reach of God”.

– “HOW OFTEN DO YOU EXPERIENCE ‘dreams’?”, with the answers being “Infrequently” and “Frequently”, is one of the questions in the “customer satisfaction survey” (conducted by, seemingly, Tenchou) in “Spotless Mind”.

– Maya’s “As The Sun Disappears” begins with a mysterious narration by an unknown narrator (presumably, Himawari) and goes quite deep into the subject of “what is real, and what is a dream” in addition to asking the question of “what will you see when you wake up”. The same monologue also curiously references “the thing beneath us, the thing above – two sides of the same coin, cut in half and separated by more distance than one can travel in a lifetime”, as the narrator says that “It will take far too long to become whole again; no matter what we do, we will always be just half of something” and wonders “how did we ever separate in the first place, getting so far apart”.

– The entire Ami’s “Somnambula” (as in, “the person who is sleep-walking”) event from the end of Chapter 2, where she and Sensei are speaking about God and Heaven while on the “bus riding backwards”.

– The mysterious “fourth entity”: the “shadow that emerges from its hole in the wall” as well as the “God that embodies everything” – that is first mentioned in “All For You” is directly related to this theme, since the narration for that event opens with a line “It sings in its sleep” (which is *also* the name of the OST playing during that scene); the same entity is likewise referenced in a similar way in “Goodnight Moon”. What’s more, just a few events prior to “All For You”, during “Where the Trees Live”, SeKaori warns Sensei that “Something is waking up” – which is then followed by him and Kaori finding Nao-chan in “First Contact”.

– The thing that both of us have already referenced from “Amy”: the fact that at the center of the Great Pareidolia Mall there is a giant frog that “occasionally wakes up from its slumber, spits out an egg and then goes back to sleep”.

– One of the lines in the opening poem from the “Eighth Eye of the Wolf Spider” reads “Circle four – the killing sleep – you've already made your choice.”

– And a bunch of other stuff from Chapter 4 that I will not list here, both to prevent potential spoilers and because this post is already far too fucking long.

So, yeah, interpret all that however you will. Like I mentioned earlier, there are many other symbolic references to “dreams” or “sleeping” that don’t seem to follow the same overarching theming of divinity/the Wishing Well: some of them simply reiterate the character’s current mental state (like the Miku example that you provided, where her dreams are “just dark” due to the fact that she is plagued by her trauma, and thus even the girl’s inner dreamscape is not an escape from all that darkness), or many similar cases where the narration states that Sensei “went to sleep/woke up feeling X”.

Pretty sure this theory is that energy is eternal and has always existed, because it can't be destroyed. So likely nothing created it either. Though when it comes to a story like this, where there are things that actually do create the worlds, I'm not sure how well this theory fits ngl. Even the xoanon only "chronicle" and not create, these universes still are created by other things. At the same time I can kind of understand if the "circle" is one big universe that houses the other universes.


So I guess those primordial beings (which I assume are before the other gods we saw) can be just as eternal as that universe? Anyway that is just food for thought by me, since I was also interested in that theory outside of this game. Especially since it seems Selebus is kind of going this route? Based on that one special event (forgot what it was) where there were different sections of worlds unrelated to them. But there are also the alternate timelines with them...that then lead to imagining more. And that's just involving the universe where Akira created Maya and then Maya made that. So alternate world of...a basically fake world. Making it is pretty complex ngl.

Very interesting honestly, I just wonder if that Sekai was the one we know, or a different one? (Not to mention it seems she is becoming more sane...). Do we really not get like more from Uta after she asks though? Since this is LiL wouldn't be surprised

Yeah, this update was actually well done.
Rewatching Kaori's event for the second time made me cry twice—when Akira keeps up that cold front the whole time but then finally breaks with "I WANT HER TO BE ALIVE I MISS HER I LOVE HER"... that contrast was really powerful.
The Uta event is kind of complicated though. Let me try to break down what happened—tell me if I got something wrong.
Before her TED talk, Sekai already pointed out that everything tonight was basically leading up to Uta finally having sex.
And honestly most of what she said was just connecting dots from earlier stuff and filling in some blanks—like the concepts of the circle
79 "The universe is a forest."
79 "We are the soil."
the xoanon


the parallel worlds thing with the 7th reset,
and that whole "beef" metaphor again. Makes you think Akira is basically like M9 wagyu to gods , right?
Regarding how the xoanon still records cancelled routes—"Still they grow and consume and eat what the gods do not"
—Sekai explained to Uta that cancelled routes are actually better because breaking away from the predetermined path (the sex route) allows her to start a new story. Sekai pointed out before her speech that Uta had already become aware of supernatural events, and finally told her to confront these things directly, to make herself important instead of living in fear—otherwise she wouldn't get the chance to learn more.
They all mentioned that breaking the cycle is impossible.



At the end of "Second Sun", akira said

So I guess if the biggest reason the gods sought Akira is to break the cycle.It might happen In the final end.

At first, Sekai said it is real. Well, obviously.

However, Uta concluded at the end that she had all known from the beginning that this is not real. Then Sekai accepted it.

OK, I'm just simply confused.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just popping in to share something simple.

Say what you will about Selebus, but I keep getting surprised by his ability to make me feel exactly when he wants me to feel. It might not be exactly what he wants me to feel, but it'll always be strong enough to make a memory.

Something about the opening of the final scene in this update really got a reaction out of me. I like Ayane as much as the next person, but I can't say I've been EXCITED to see that I would be spending time with her in particular. There was something predictable about her and her scenes I guess.

With the recent revelations and adventures I was impressed and intrigued, but that feeling remained. I didn't think I was any further bonded to Ayane than I have been. The moment I saw Ayane's little blue name tag show up when I knocked on Sana's door I felt a wave of joy like she she'd turned up after being missing for weeks while I've been worried sick. And as the innocence of the scene's first moments played out, I understood for a fleeting moment the love that Selebus has for her and his characters and the love that she draws to herself from so many of us in the community.

That's all really. Surrounded by all this drama and depravity, the thing that shocked me was a corset and smile./SPOILER]

When filling the gap in regards to "how? what?", it feels just like same classic mumble jumble crap, dishing out more argument than there really is in a lore dumping fashion because it's not within Selly's ability to do this in subtle buiild-up sequences. Maybe it was possible back in the days when there were only 3 gods at play, when Selly maybe really had a complicated but already completed diagram about all these shit. Now I just believe otherwise and hope for the day that finally proves me wrong will come.

But back to the part that still interests me tons. I care not what Sekai's TED talk is about, but rather why Sekai herself does any of this. The first ELATION PROTOCOL is confusing as hell but somehow the second one makes a linear regression between these two events almost possible: two girls with barely any "progress" receive a out-of-nowhere Sekai infestation, which seemingly serves the purpose of "hastening the pace".

"Purpose" was the reason I thought Tsuneyo's ELATION PROTOCOL was bizarre before this newfound similarity to Uta's. Back then it felt that Sekai only did what she did to Tsuneyo because Selly needed 1) readers to face Lavender Green's reality(?), and 2) a Tsuneyo "sex scene" because it's been too long without one. Selly needed that while Sekai did not.

But now, Sekai does hint something by the end of Uta's ELATION PROTOCOL, that her intervention does mean something. It is perhaps a very personal goal that can only be accomplished when more or all girls become aware and/or become dicked by Aki-kun. And this somehow feels very relevant to what Ami Prime has been doing recently, presenting a drugged Karin to Sensei and mentioning Rin all to reemphasize the fact that "Akira really needs to fuck everyone so that something can be done". It also feels like a right incentive Ami can gladly oblige if that something directly involves Sekai (and Sensei maybe; we won't be sure whether Sekai does this for her ghostly self or for her precious Aki-kun in a beyond the grave big picture way).


Anyway, two dots always form a straight line so take this with a grain of salt unless there really is a third ELATION PROTOCOL that miraculously falls in the same line (maybe another someone with no progress with/without suppressed urges toward Akira? Otoha?)

spoilers.title: Scattered thoughts
spoilers.html:
Haven't finished reading all relevant posts so I am not sure if anyone would be with me, but despite the blatant reveal Sekai delivered, I am ever so slightly disappointed. Sekai's TED talk pretty much only sums up to "letting Uta check out the bad ending and reaffirming Uta the supernatural nature of Kumon-mi". When filling the gap in regards to "how? what?", it feels just like same classic mumble jumble crap, dishing out more argument than there really is in a lore dumping fashion because it's not within Selly's ability to do this in subtle buiild-up sequences. Maybe it was possible back in the days when there were only 3 gods at play, when Selly maybe really had a complicated but already completed diagram about all these shit. Now I just believe otherwise and hope for the day that finally proves me wrong will come.

But back to the part that still interests me tons. I care not what Sekai's TED talk is about, but rather why Sekai herself does any of this. The first ELATION PROTOCOL is confusing as hell but somehow the second one makes a linear regression between these two events almost possible: two girls with barely any "progress" receive a out-of-nowhere Sekai infestation, which seemingly serves the purpose of "hastening the pace".

"Purpose" was the reason I thought Tsuneyo's ELATION PROTOCOL was bizarre before this newfound similarity to Uta's. Back then it felt that Sekai only did what she did to Tsuneyo because Selly needed 1) readers to face Lavender Green's reality(?), and 2) a Tsuneyo "sex scene" because it's been too long without one. Selly needed that while Sekai did not.

But now, Sekai does hint something by the end of Uta's ELATION PROTOCOL, that her intervention does mean something. It is perhaps a very personal goal that can only be accomplished when more or all girls become aware and/or become dicked by Aki-kun. And this somehow feels very relevant to what Ami Prime has been doing recently, presenting a drugged Karin to Sensei and mentioning Rin all to reemphasize the fact that "Akira really needs to fuck everyone so that something can be done". It also feels like a right incentive Ami can gladly oblige if that something directly involves Sekai (and Sensei maybe; we won't be sure whether Sekai does this for her ghostly self or for her precious Aki-kun in a beyond the grave big picture way).


Anyway, two dots always form a straight line so take this with a grain of salt unless there really is a third ELATION PROTOCOL that miraculously falls in the same line (maybe another someone with no progress with/without suppressed urges toward Akira? Otoha?)

The wording used here is, admittedly, extremely ambiguous, which I don't think was really the intention on Selebus' part, but my personal understanding of this apparent "contradiction" is that the "there will be no more 'Resets' like you call them" line specifically refers to the point in time *after* "someone like me is going to come and cleanse it" rather than just being a universal statement.

So the intended takeaway from Himawari's statement seems to be that once one of the other custodians (or a high-ranking God) finally decides to pull the plug on Terminal 23 (which is going to happen sooner rather than later), *then* there are going to be no further Resets, but *until* that point they are still going to keep happening like usual, which explains why Akira is currently anticipating the next one.

Besides, from a writing standpoint, getting rid of the safety net and core narrative framework that are the Resets at this present moment in the story would be *very* premature, in my opinion, as this is an insanely big shift in the previously-established paradigm that should be explicitly reserved for some insanely big climactic moment, heralding the point of no return – like the beginning of the Dark Route, for example. Currently, we are not anywhere close to being on *that* level of narrative magnitude yet, so I'm fully expecting that the Resets are going to persist through the remainder of Chapter 4 and also probably through the entirety of Chapter 5, as well – though if I'm wrong, this is certaingly going to be an interesting twist.
